lines.text: Fifty summers ago. The pines are young, the hearthstone is clean, and the hands are yours, but younger.
You say it aloud, to nobody: "Three pines, a lake, and nobody. This'll do."

steps.objective: Take wood from the fallen pine: break its logs with the axe.
Lay the wood on the hearthstone: right-click it with the logs.
Light it: flint and steel on the wood.

lines.text: The fire takes. Out on the water, something moves under the still.

steps.objective: Catch a fish in the water with the rod.
Cook it on the fire: right-click the fire with the fish.

choices.reply: At first light you kick out the fire and shoulder your pack.

lines.text: The fish spits on the fire. A loon calls across the water, and nothing answers it.
You could stay. Nobody would know.

steps.objective: Choose: press its number.

done.text: One notch, for this summer. You walk on, whistling.

lines.text: Before you go, you look back at the middle pine.

steps.objective: Cut a notch in the middle pine: right-click its trunk with the axe.

lines.text: Twenty winters ago. Lamps burn down the length of the hall, and on the stone the shard hums.
Your sleeve is grey. Along the walls, people sleep in their furs.

steps.objective: Lift the shard from the stone: right-click it.

done.text: Below you, grey coats come up the snow at a run, axes out. They pass you without a look.
Behind you, up at the stair, the shouting stops.

lines.text: Someone sits up in the furs. Then another. A shout, in words you don't know.
Run.

steps.objective: Get out: up the stair and away from the hall.

choices.reply: You pull your arm free.

lines.text: A hand catches your arm. An old woman, barefoot in the snow, who came down another way.
Please.

steps.objective: Choose: press its number.

lines.text: A grey coat comes down the slope, wiping his axe in the snow.
Well, finder?
You tell him: "Empty. Someone beat us to it."

steps.objective: Hear him out.

lines.text: That night you walk east, alone, with the shard against your chest.
A day on, you come to a lake frozen white. You cut down through the ice and let the shard sink.
On a stone by the shore you cut your sign: a circle, and a line through it.

steps.objective: Remember.

lines.text: Forty-five summers ago. The hall smells of dust and old smoke, and on the stone the shard hums.
Your hands are young. Your ember burns bright.

steps.objective: Lift the shard from the stone: right-click it.

done.text: Out on the green, a handful of people are digging in the ashes of the old houses, with spades and a handcart.
Far off on the ridge, riders in grey sit their horses and watch the plain.

lines.text: Up the well, voices, and the ring of a spade on stone.

steps.objective: Climb up out of the well.

lines.text: More of it here. Pots, a lamp, a bell gone green. All bronze.
Every bit of it goes in the pot. Tollbridge will have a bell of its own.
A bell, and we're a town. Not a ford with a toll on it.
Nobody asks who you are. A traveller warming his hands at a casting fire is nothing new.

steps.objective: Remember.

choices.reply: You wait for their backs to turn.

lines.text: On the ridge, the riders turn their horses this way. The shard is warm against your chest.
A pack gets searched. Nobody searches a bell.

steps.objective: Choose: press its number.

done.text: The bronze takes it without a sound.

lines.text: They turn away to carry the mould up from the cart.

steps.objective: Drop the shard into the melt: right-click it.

lines.text: You stay to watch them pour it. When it's cool they hang it from a pole and ring it, and the whole crossing comes up the river to hear.
On the ridge the riders listen a while. Then they ride on.

steps.objective: Remember.

lines.text: Thirty winters ago. Your feet hurt. The fire is small.
Men in grey sit down across the flames. They are kind. They have been kind for a long time.
The road's long, finder. Nobody would blame you for sitting a while.

steps.objective: Sit by the fire.

lines.text: A girl in grey comes round the fire with a loaf, and holds it out with both hands.
A tiny open eye is stitched on her coat.

steps.objective: Choose: press its number.

lines.text: You know this bread. You've eaten it: dark and sweet, an eye pressed into the crust.
You know this bread. A loaf like it is wrapped in your pack.
You know this bread. You fed a loaf like it to a fire once.
She watches you eat every crumb, and smiles.

steps.objective: Eat.

lines.text: In the morning you write in the journal: "Tomorrow I will walk on."
The fire goes out. You don't walk on.

steps.objective: Remember.

lines.text: Thirty-five winters ago. A spear in your hand, the ember warm in the other, and the sand very still.
The sand heaves. An eye opens in the dune, as big as a door.

steps.objective: Stand your ground.

done.text: Behind you, over the dunes, someone is laughing. Then a whole camp of them, and somebody starts to sing.

lines.text: Run.

steps.objective: Run: get away from the bowl.

lines.text: Twenty-five winters ago. The house is new and smells of sawdust. Your ember is small, and you keep it in your fist.
A girl in grey sits by the hearth with her knees drawn up, watching your hand.

steps.objective: Sit by the hearth.

choices.text: Send her back to the others.

lines.text: She whispers to your fist, as if something in it could hear.
The coal brightens between your fingers.

steps.objective: Choose: press its number.

lines.text: You tell her it listens, and that it's the one thing in the world that never lies to you.
She talks to it until she falls asleep by the hearth. You sit up with it till morning.

steps.objective: Remember.

lines.text: The last night. You are him: old, cold, coughing, the fire low. The ember is the size of a pea.
You can feel what it wants. You've been too tired to say no for a long time.

steps.objective: Sit by the fire.

choices.text: Let it go out with you.

lines.text: A face comes down the road towards the fire: young, frightened, alone.
You know what you're carrying. You know what it wants. There is nobody else.

steps.objective: Choose: press its number.

lines.text: You press the ember into their hand. Under the voice that has worn yours for thirty winters, faint, older, your own: "...don't let it look at them..."

steps.objective: Remember.

morwen.name: Morwen
remarks: Sleep while the sun's up. That's when we do.

nell.name: Nell
remarks: Twenty winters. I can wait a few days more.

pilgrim.name: Hesper
remarks: They'll let us in. They have to.

remarks: Sit. The fire's warm. That's all a man needs.

remarks: Don't look at me like that. I saw what I saw.

tide_warden_1.name: A warden
remarks: I don't know why. I just did.

tide_warden_2.name: A warden
remarks: Don't ask me. My knees asked.

warden.name: The warden
remarks: The ward holds. For now.

wil.name: Wil
remarks: Mind the hoops. They roll.

wren.name: Wren
remarks: I'm not tired. I'm not.

choices.reply: Nobody, now. A man who walked too little and stopped too long.
By my fire. Off the road, where nobody comes.

lines.text: You wake on cold ground beside a fire. You don't remember lying down. You don't remember anything before this fire.
An old man sits across the flames, propped against a log. His face is grey, and his breath rattles.
There you are. Thought I'd go before you woke.

steps.objective: Sit with the stranger.

people.stranger: An old man who found me by the road and brought me to his fire. He was dying.

story: I woke by a stranger's fire. I don't know my name, or how I came to be there.

choices.reply: Better than you'd like. Don't ask me how. There isn't time.
Good. Names are for people who stay.
choices.text: I don't know my own name.

lines.text: I found you lying by the road and brought you here. It took the last of what I had.
Don't look at me like that. I'm dying, that's all. I'm old, and I walked further than I had left in me.
His shirt is open at the collar. An old white scar runs across his chest, over the heart.
Let me look at you. ...Yes. It's you, then.

steps.objective: Sit with the stranger.

people.stranger: He said bringing me to his fire took the last of his strength. He knew my face, and wouldn't say how. An old white scar ran over his heart.

choices.reply: That's all I need.
choices.story: I told him I'd carry it.

choices.reply: Nobody does, at first. Carry it anyway.
choices.story: I told him I didn't even know who I was. He said to carry it anyway.
choices.text: I don't even know who I am.

lines.text: He fumbles at his belt and holds out a closed fist. It shakes.
Hold out your hand.
He presses something into your palm: a coal no bigger than a thumb, grey and cold as a stone.
That's an ember. Mine. It's been cold for years.
Walk with it and it wakes. It lives on what you see: new ground, every day.
Three things, and I won't have the breath to say them twice.
Walk every day. A cold ember is no use to anyone.
Never stay long in one place. Stay, and something finds you.

steps.objective: Sit with the stranger.
story: He gave me his ember, cold as a stone, and told me to walk with it.

words.ember: What the stranger gave me: an ember, a coal no bigger than a thumb, cold as a stone. He said it wakes if I walk with it, and that it lives on what I see.

lines.text: He coughs for a long time. When he looks up, he looks past you, at something that isn't there.
Don't let it... the shards. I took them. Don't let it have...

steps.objective: Sit with the stranger.

people.stranger: He died before I learned his name.

story: He died before he could finish: "Don't let it... the shards. I took them. Don't let it have..." I don't know what he meant.

choices.text: Here rests a good man, who gave all he had.

His pack lies by the fire. He won't need it now.

lines.text: The fire pops. The old man is dead.
You can't leave him here for the crows.

steps.objective: Bury him.
story: I buried him by his fire. On his stone I wrote: "{stone}"
steps.unwritten: I buried him by his fire, and left his stone bare. I didn't know what to write.

quests.summary: I woke by a stranger's fire with no name and no memory of the road. He is dying, and he wants to talk.
quests.title: The Last Fire

done.text: The land here is new to you. The coal in your hand is a little less cold.

lines.text: He knew your face. You don't. All he left you is a cold coal and three rules.
It wakes on new ground, he said. Maybe it remembers what you can't.

steps.objective: Find new ground for the ember: {left} blocks to go.
story: I walked away from his fire. He knew who I was, and the ember is all I have of that, so I took it somewhere new.

lines.text: The sun is getting low. His last rule comes back to you: never sleep in the open. A tent, with a fire by it.

steps.objective: Pitch your tent, light a campfire beside it, and rest by the fire.
story: I made my first camp: my tent, and a fire beside it.

done.text: The ember in your hand grows warm. Then, for the first time, it glows.
Over the ridge ahead, smoke. Under it, the sky is red.
The ember leans in your palm, the way a needle leans, towards the smoke.

lines.text: You sit by your fire. The shadows stretch, and the sky goes gold, then red.

steps.objective: Rest by your fire.
story: At dusk the ember woke in my hand. It had seen new land, the way he said it would.
Then I saw the smoke over the ridge.

words.ember: It woke on my first evening on the road. It's warm now, it glows, and it leans towards where I'm meant to go.

quests.summary: He knew my face, and the ember might know the rest. Take it to new ground, and make a camp of my own before dark.
quests.title: The First Day

steps.awake: Not tonight. The sky over the ridge is red.

done.text: The town burns. Roofs have fallen in, and nothing moves but the fire.

steps.objective: Go to the burning town, tonight.

steps.awake: Not here. Not among the dead.

clues.text: A man by the well. His shirt is torn open over the heart. His purse is still on his belt.
A woman in a doorway, opened the same way. Her rings are still on her hands.

Tracks of many feet, out of the dark and back into it. None of them carried anything away.
The bell tower stands, black but whole. Under it, behind a cellar door, someone is crying.

lines.text: In the smoke, the ember throbs in your fist, as if it wants to be held up.

hob: One more step and I'll swing.

steps.awake: Not now. Someone is crying under the bell tower.

choices.reply: Mam said Wayfarers aren't real.

choices.text: I don't know what I am.

people.hob: The smith of Tollbridge, big and frightened, and the first to see I was only a person.

Hold the door!

pip: Is it over? Is it morning?

done.text: The drift opens into a hall, cut square and high. On a stone at its far end, something hums.

lines.text: Cold air breathes out of the dark. Someone dug this a long time ago, and went a long way down.

steps.objective: Go down into the old tunnels, where the ember pulls.
story: It led me to old tunnels under a forest, and down.

done.text: A warmth runs up your arm, and then a voice you last heard dying:
Well. That's one.
Don't look so surprised. Did you think I'd let you carry it alone?
You heard me at the fire. The shards. Gather them, bring them to a frame, and we put its eye out for good.
A frame. You'll know one when you see it. No more burning towns.
When you look down, old tracks stand out on the ground, as if the ember held them up for you.

lines.text: On the stone lies a sliver of something like dark glass. It hums, and the ember in your hand hums back.

steps.objective: Take it from the stone: right-click it.

people.stranger: His voice came back with the first shard. Nobody else hears it. He wants the shards brought to a frame, to put out "its eye".

story: In a hall at the bottom of the tunnels lay a shard. When I took it, it sank into the ember, and the stranger spoke to me. He's dead. I heard him anyway.

words.shards: The first lay on a stone in a hall under the forest, humming. It sank into the ember, and his voice came with it.

lines.text: Go on, back to your caravan. Don't mind me. I'll be quiet. Mostly.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

lines.text: You came back different. What's in that hand now?
She can't hear me. Only you can.
The ember was mine once. Now it's yours, and it seems I came with it.
I made my first camp by a lake, under three pines. It's to the {direction} of here. I'd like to see it again.

steps.objective: Sit with Tamsin at the caravan's fire.
story: At the caravan's fire his voice told me where he made his first camp: by a lake, under three pines, to the {direction}. He wants to see it again.

quests.summary: The ember pulls towards something far ahead, and it won't say where. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: The Pull

done.text: Three pines over still water. Under them, a ring of stones gone green, and the bones of a lean-to.
Three pines. They were smaller.

steps.objective: Find his first camp, by a lake under three pines.
story: He led me to a lake under three pines, where he made his first camp.

clues.text: Notches cut into the middle pine, one above the next, the oldest grown over with bark. Somebody came back here, summer after summer.
A stake at the water's edge, a rotten line still knotted round it. Somebody fished here.
A flat hearthstone in the ring, black with old fires. Cut into it, long after the soot, is an open eye.

done.text: That stone. Touch it. I want to see it the way it was.

lines.text: Whoever sat here, sat here often. Hold up the ember: it shows what he left.

steps.objective: Look at what he left, with the ember held up: {found}/{needed}.

done.text: You stand at the hearthstone again. The eye is cut into it, as before.
I was happy here.
...Wait. That sack wasn't there.

steps.objective: Touch the hearthstone: right-click it.

people.stranger: He was young once, and happy. At his first camp I made camp as him, and I wanted to stay. He walked on.

story: When I touched the hearthstone, the ember flared, and I was him, young, making camp under three young pines. I wanted to stay one more summer. He didn't.

clues.text: A sack, dry, as if it was set down days ago. Inside: bread, dried fish, and a folded note.

done.text: The note: "For whoever carries his light now. Eat. - M."
...Someone's been here. Someone who knows my camps.

steps.objective: Look in the sack under the lean-to: right-click it.

reward.claimed: You pack the bread and the fish, and keep the note.
reward.text: bread, dried fish, and a note signed M.
reward.title: Under the Lean-to

story: Under his lean-to someone had left bread, dried fish and a note signed M. Somebody knew I'd come.

lines.text: Back to the caravan. I've seen what I wanted to see.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

quests.summary: The voice wants to see the camp he made when he first set out, by a lake under three pines. Find it.
quests.title: His First Camp

steps.objective: Watch the road for whatever M. leaves next.
story: Someone signing themselves M. leaves food where he used to camp. They knew I would come.

clues.text: A barrel by the way, its lid tied down. Inside: bread, dried fish, and a folded note.

done.text: The note: "Across the sea already. He'd have been proud of you, the old fool. Eat something warm tonight. - M."

lines.text: Someone's set something down by the way, ahead of us. The same hand as before, I'd say.

steps.objective: Find what M. left by the way, and open it: right-click it.

reward.claimed: You pack the bread and the fish, and keep the note.
reward.text: bread, dried fish, and a note signed M.
reward.title: By the Way

story: M. left a barrel by the way across the sea: bread, dried fish and a note. She crossed before we did.

steps.objective: Watch the road for whatever M. leaves next.
story: M. leaves food by the way wherever we go. I wonder how far she'll follow.

clues.text: Another barrel by the way, the rope on it older. Bread, fish, and a note in the same hand.

done.text: The note, in the same hand: "You fly now. I never could keep up with him either. Eat. He never ate enough either. - M."

lines.text: Another one. She's still following, after everything.

steps.objective: Find what M. left by the way, and open it: right-click it.

reward.claimed: You pack the bread and the fish, and keep the note.
reward.text: bread, dried fish, and a last note signed M.
reward.title: The Last Bundle

story: M. left one last barrel by the way. Her note says he never ate enough either.

quests.summary: Someone left food under his lean-to, with a note signed M. They know his camps, and they know someone carries his light now.
quests.title: The Gifts

done.text: A horn sounds across the water, low and long.

lines.text: The ember tugs at your hand again: steady, patient, towards something a long way off.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The morning after his first camp, the ember pulled again, towards something far ahead.

done.text: Across the water a horn calls twice. The last of the men in grey turn and climb back towards the hill.

steps.failed: The wounded man goes down in the shallows, and doesn't get up.

lines.text: A man stumbles out of the far trees and into the ford, holding his side. He leaves red in the water.
There! The ember! Take them both!
Fight or run. Don't just stand there.

steps.objective: Keep the wounded man alive while they come across the ford.

corin: Keep them in the water. They're slow in the water.
I can't stand. Don't let them reach me.

story: At a river ford, men in grey came across the water after a wounded man, and after the ember. We held the bank.
steps.wave: They come across the ford: {wave} of {waves}

choices.reply: Thank you. I mean it. I'll keep up, or I'll keep quiet.
choices.text: Come with us. You won't get far alone.

choices.reply: I've kept up with worse than you. Lead on.

lines.text: They'll be back with more. They always come back with more.
Let me see your hand. ...That light.
I know that light. I'd know it anywhere.
Corin. Don't thank me. I brought them.
They're Gazebound. My own company, until last night.
Their heir wants that coal more than he wants me. And he wants me badly.
He pulls his shirt open. Over his heart runs an old white scar, like the one on the old man by the fire.
We all carry one. They let the night look into you. If you live, it never looks again.
The man who carried that light before you. I served under him, six winters.
Don't ask me his name. Not yet.
Where are you walking? Can a man with one good leg walk with you?

steps.objective: Talk to the wounded man by the ford.

people.corin: A deserter from the men in grey, with their scar over his heart. He served under the stranger for six winters, and won't say his name. We held the ford for him.

story: The man was Corin, a deserter. He knew the ember's light, and the man who carried it before me, and he wouldn't say his name. He walks with us now.

words.gazebound: Men in grey who hunt whoever carries an ember. Every one of them has a scar over the heart, as the stranger had. Corin was one of them.
words.heir: Whoever leads the Gazebound. Corin says he wants the ember more than anything, and Corin ran from him.

lines.text: Go on ahead. I'll follow your smoke. I'm good at following smoke.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

lines.text: You brought one of the men in grey to our fire.
Not one of them. Not any more.
The man who had that ember before you. Where is he?
You tell him about the old man's fire, and the grave beside it.
He's dead, then. Good.
...No. Not good.
My brother's still up at that outpost above the ford. He took the scar the same night I did.
Not now. When you're stronger. I'll tell you when.

steps.objective: Talk to Corin, by his tent at the edge of the camp.

people.corin: Corin heard the stranger is dead, and said good, and then said no. His brother is still with the Gazebound.

story: At the caravan's fire Corin heard the stranger was dead. He said good, and then he said no. His brother is still with the Gazebound, at the outpost above the ford.

quests.summary: The ember pulls again, as it pulled to the old tunnels. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: The Deserter

steps.objective: Wait for Corin's word: he'll say when you're ready.
story: Corin's brother took the Gazebound's scar the same night Corin did, and still serves at the outpost above the ford. Corin will say when.

lines.text: His company crossed before us. They camp at an outpost on this shore, a day off.
Brannoc. My brother. If he comes, he comes. If he won't, I want to hear it from you.

steps.objective: Hear Corin out at the fire.

people.corin: His brother Brannoc's company crossed the sea before us and camps at an outpost on this shore.

story: Corin's brother Brannoc camps with his company at an outpost on this shore. Corin asked me to fetch him, or hear him say no.

done.text: Smoke over the trees, and a banner with an open eye on it.

steps.objective: Find the Gazebound outpost on this shore.
story: Brannoc's company camps at a Gazebound outpost a day from the caravan.

lines.text: The ember! Up, all of you!

steps.objective: Hold against the outpost's men.
story: The outpost's men came down on us, and we held.

choices.reply: Then tell him I'm well. Tell him I'm sorry about the ford.
choices.story: I told Brannoc that Corin's alive and asked for him. Tell him I'm well, he said.
choices.text: Corin's alive. He asked for you.

choices.reply: No.
choices.story: I asked Brannoc to come with us. He said no.

done.text: He turns and walks up the hill, and doesn't look back.

lines.text: A man in grey stands below the tower, unarmed, watching you come.
Brannoc. You're the one Corin follows now.
I chose it. The scar, the quiet. He chose the road; I chose the quiet. Nothing looks for me any more.

steps.objective: Find Corin's brother at the outpost.

people.brannoc: Corin's brother. He took the Gazebound's scar willingly and doesn't want to be saved.

story: Corin's brother Brannoc took the scar willingly. He chose the quiet, he said, and doesn't want to be saved.

done.text: He's well. Good.
Corin doesn't say anything else all evening.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke, and tell Corin.
story: I told Corin his brother is well and won't come. He said good, and nothing else all evening.

quests.summary: Corin's brother serves the Gazebound. Corin will say when the team is strong enough to fetch him.
quests.title: His Brother

done.text: Under the mangroves the water goes black and still. At its edge stands a hut on stilts, smoke at its chimney, and three women watch you from the porch.

forced.text: Something foul splashes over you. Your arms and legs go heavy.

steps.forced_story: I went down into their water without the witches' leave, and they turned on me for it.

lines.text: The ember tugs again, the same way as before the ford, as if the ford had only been in the way.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The morning after the ford, the ember pulled on, the way it had pulled before the horn.

choices.reply: Hold still.
Suit yourself. But nobody goes down there without our leave.

done.text: She takes your chin in a cold hand and looks into your eyes. Then she flinches back, as if the ember had burnt her.
Something looks out of you.
...Not his, then. Whatever you are.
Go down, if it wants you. Under the water, where it shows you no face.
Drink this first, or the bog keeps you.

forced.text: Something foul splashes over you. Your arms and legs go heavy.

steps.forced_story: I went down into their water without the witches' leave, and they turned on me for it.

lines.text: That's far enough. We know that light.
A man carried it here once. He sat on this porch and swore by it, and his word was worth less than the mud.
He got what he came for. We got two huts burned.
I'm Rue. That's Sedge, and the girl is Tansy.
The Marsh Mothers kept this water before us, and we keep it still. Go back the way you came.
Wait. Let me look at you.

steps.objective: Talk to the old woman on the porch.

people.rue: The eldest of three witches who keep a hut over a black pool. She curses the man who carried this ember before me: he swore by it, and broke his word.
people.sedge: The second of the witches, hard as a root. The man who carried this ember cost them two huts, and she hasn't forgiven it.
people.tansy: The youngest of the witches. She looked into my eyes and flinched. Something looks out of me, she said.

rue: Go down, or go home. Don't stand on my porch.
sedge: Mind where you put your feet. The bog keeps what it gets.
tansy: Don't look at me like that. I saw what I saw.

reward.claimed: You tuck the bottle away. It smells of the swamp.
reward.text: A stoppered bottle that smells of the swamp. Drink it before you go under, and the water lets you breathe a while.
reward.title: The witches' brew

story: In a swamp the ember led me to three witches at a black pool. They know this light, and hate the man who carried it. The youngest looked into me and flinched, and they let me go down.

words.marsh_mothers: Whoever kept the black pool before the witches. The witches keep it now, and won't say what lies under it.

done.text: You come up out of black water into air that smells of earth: a hall, dry, sunk in the mud. On a stone at its heart something hums.

lines.text: Witches. They'd curse the rain for falling. Go on, then. Down you go.

steps.objective: Drink the brew, then go down into the black pool and follow the ember.

rue: You've had your leave. Go down.
sedge: Mind where you put your feet. The bog keeps what it gets.
tansy: Hold the light up when you're under. It knows the way better than you do.

story: Under the black pool a drowned tunnel led to a dry hall, sunk in the mud.

asking.text: The shard hums on its stone. Up on the porch the fisher is sitting up, because of whatever hums down here.

choices.reply: You close your hand on it.
You leave it humming on its stone.

reward.claimed: You stow the bottles. They're warm.
reward.text: Two of the witches' bottles, brewed from the black water. Drink one when a wound won't close.
reward.title: The witches' brews

closes.the_witches_debt: The black pool is only water now. There was nothing left to brew with, and the fisher's fever was his own to fight.

lines.text: On the stone lies a sliver like the first, humming, and the ember hums back.

steps.objective: Take it from the stone: right-click it.
story: In the hall under the black pool lay a second shard.

words.shards: The second lay on a stone in a hall under a black pool in the swamp, where the witches keep their hut.

done.text: The stair ends behind a wall that is no wall, in a cellar of roots. A ladder, a hatch, and you come up into a room that smells of smoke.
All these years we kept the door, and never knew it.
And the pool's gone flat as rain water. Whatever you took, it was ours.

lines.text: Two. They'd have sat on it forever, brewing over it.
Beside the stone, a stretch of mud wall goes faint as smoke. Behind it, steps climb into the dark.

steps.objective: Go up the stair behind the faint wall.
story: Taking the shard showed me a wall that was no wall: the Marsh Mothers' own stair, up into the witches' cellar. Their pool has been plain water since.

words.true_sight: Since the second shard I see through what isn't there: a wall that's only seeming shows faint as smoke.

done.text: The stair ends behind a wall that is no wall, in a cellar of roots. A ladder, a hatch, and you come up into a room that smells of smoke.
All these years we kept the door, and never knew it.
You paid his debt and took our water. Then we're even, you and I.

lines.text: Two. They'd have sat on it forever, brewing over it.
Beside the stone, a stretch of mud wall goes faint as smoke. Behind it, steps climb into the dark.

steps.objective: Go up the stair behind the faint wall.
story: I took the shard, knowing what it cost the witches. It showed me the Marsh Mothers' own stair, up into their cellar.

words.true_sight: Since the second shard I see through what isn't there: a wall that's only seeming shows faint as smoke.

done.text: You left it.
Then the water's still ours, and so's our door, light-bearer, whenever you need it.

lines.text: Soft. That's one fewer at the gate.

steps.objective: Swim back up through the black pool.
story: I left the shard on its stone, for the witches' cups. The stranger called it soft.

lines.text: Back to your caravan. Mind the bog on the way out.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

quests.summary: The ember pulls on, the way it pulled before the horn at the ford. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: Still Water

clues.text: A blue orchid on the bank, the one Rue wanted.
Frogspawn at the water's edge, cold and quick.
A worn step at the pool's edge, where they dip their bottles. You fill one with black water.

lines.text: That man came up our water two days ago, burning. We've nothing left to brew with.
A blue orchid, frogspawn, and a bottle of the black water. My knees won't take me round the pool any more.
The one who carried that light owes us. You can pay some of it.

steps.objective: Find what the brew needs round the pool: a blue orchid, frogspawn and the black water.

people.fisher: A fisher from somewhere downriver, burning with fever on the witches' porch.

story: A fisher lay fevered on the witches' porch. Rue sent me round the pool for what their brew needs.

lines.text: Rue boils it all in the porch cauldron and spoons it into the fisher, a sip at a time.
...Cold. Why's it cold?
You hold up the ember. The brew in the cup glows faintly, the way the pool glows.
Whatever heals is down there. It always was.
That's his debt paid. Yours is your own.

steps.objective: Bring what you found to Rue on the porch.
story: I found what the witches' brew needed, and the fisher sat up. Whatever heals in their pool lies down there, with the shard.

quests.summary: A fisher lies fevered on the witches' porch, and they have nothing left to brew with. Find what the brew needs round the black pool, with the ember held up.
quests.title: The Witches' Debt

road.text: Someone's walked in your smoke since my first camp. Don't look round.

steps.awake: Not yet. Sit by the fire a while.

choices.reply: Names are for people who stay.
choices.story: She wouldn't give her name. Names are for people who stay, she said.

choices.reply: Someone had to. You walk like he did, and he forgot to eat.
choices.story: She was the one who left the bread at his first camp.
choices.text: You left the bread at his camp.

choices.reply: I'm going. I only came to see who carries it now.
choices.story: I told her to get away from our fire. She went.

done.text: Eat. You walk further on bread.
She sets a loaf on the log beside her and stands.
The fire gusts. Smoke rolls over the circle, and when it thins she is gone.
The loaf is still on the log, dark and round.

lines.text: Someone walks out of the dark and sits down across the fire. A grey hood, a grey coat, an eye stitched over the heart.
Gazebound. At my fire.
Hob gets up with his hammer in his fist. Nobody else moves.
So he's dead. I knew his smoke before I knew your face.

steps.objective: Sit at the caravan's fire.

people.maren: A hooded woman in Gazebound grey. She knew the stranger's smoke, and that he was dead. She left us bread.

story: A woman in Gazebound grey walked out of the dark and sat down at our fire. She knew the stranger's smoke, and that he was dead. Then she was gone in the smoke, and left a loaf behind.

steps.awake: Not yet. Her bread is still on the log.

choices.story: I ate her bread. It was good.

choices.reply: You wrap it in a cloth for the road.

choices.story: I kept her bread for the road.

choices.reply: Waste.
choices.story: I gave her bread to the fire. The stranger called it a waste.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The morning after the hooded woman's visit, the ember pulled towards the snow.

done.text: The tracks end at a long, low house of stone and hide, half buried in the snow.
An arrow thuds into the snow by your boot.

steps.objective: Follow the tracks.
story: Across my way ran a hunter's tracks, dragging something that bled. I followed them to a house half buried in the snow.

lines.text: That's close enough. Hold the fire up where I can see it.
A woman in furs stands on the roof, an arrow on the string. She looks at the ember in your hand for a long breath.
...A Wayfarer's fire. Twenty winters I've waited for one of those.
I'm Nell. The last of the Frost Walkers.
Twenty winters ago I came home from a hunt and found my people dead on the stair to our hall. The hall was empty.
Our stone down there remembers what it saw. It shows it only to a Wayfarer's fire.
Wake it for me. I want a name.
She climbs down and puts a pair of snowshoes in your hands: bent ash, laced with gut, worn smooth.
Up there you'd sink to the waist in those boots. My mother made these.
I'll be at the stair at first light. Don't make me wait.

steps.objective: Hear out the woman on the roof.

people.nell: Nell, the last of the Frost Walkers. She came home from a hunt twenty winters ago to find her people dead on their hall's stair. She wants a name.

reward.claimed: You lace them on. They grip the snow like a hand.

items.name: Frost Walkers' Snowshoes
items.tooltip: Nell's mother made them. Worn with your charms, they carry you over powder snow, and faster over snow.

reward.text: a pair of snowshoes Nell's mother made: bent ash, laced with gut. They carry you over powder snow.

story: On the roof stood Nell, the last of the Frost Walkers, with an arrow for me until she saw the ember. Her people died on their hall's stair twenty winters ago, and their stone was emptied. She wants a name, and gave me her mother's snowshoes for the way up.

words.frost_walkers: Nell's people. They wintered in a hall up in the deep snow, with a stone that remembers. All dead but her.

lines.text: Go on to your people. I'll come and look at them before dark.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

lines.text: Your hunter came in at dusk. Sat down at the edge of the light and counted us. Twice.
I like to know who I'm sleeping near.
She can stay. Anyone who brings meat can stay.

steps.objective: Sit with Tamsin at the caravan's fire.
story: Nell came to the caravan's fire that evening, and counted us.

lines.text: She looked at my coat for a long time.

steps.objective: Talk to Corin, by his tent at the edge of the camp.

Keep it. Every one you leave behind is one the gaze can take back.
Up at the edge of the hole, Nell waits with her hand out.

choices.reply: You close your hand on it. Nell turns away.
choices.story: I kept the shard. Nell turned away.

choices.reply: You put it in her hand. She holds it a long time, then walks off along the shore without a word.
choices.story: I gave the shard to Nell, to bury with her people. She walked off along the shore without a word.

lines.text: That's it. Cut it out, and give it to me. I'll bury it with them.
The ice is old and deep. The shape under it will take a pickaxe to reach.

steps.objective: Cut down through the ice to the shard, then right-click it.
story: Under the ice lay the third shard, where he sank it.

words.shards: The third lay under the ice of a lake a day east of the Frost Walkers' hall, where he sank it twenty winters ago.

lines.text: The shard sinks into the ember. The dark under the ice thins, as if your eyes had grown used to it.
Three. She'll hate you for it. Better her than the gaze.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

words.dark_sight: Since the third shard the dark shows me what's in it, dimly: enough to find my way through a cave without a torch.

lines.text: Soft. That's one the gaze can come for.

steps.objective: Wait for Nell's word.
story: Nell will bury her people's names on their old winter grounds. She said she'd send word.

arrived.text: Here. They wintered here, before the hall. I was born here.

lines.text: There you are. My people wintered on this shore once, in the snow. I'll lay their names there.
Walk with me. I don't want to do it alone.

steps.objective: Walk Nell to her people's old winter grounds.
story: Nell asked me to walk with her to her people's old winter grounds on this shore, to lay their names to rest.

choices.reply: Then he left late.
choices.story: I told Nell that Corin left them. Then he left late, she said.

choices.reply: You say nothing. She doesn't need you to.
choices.story: I said nothing at the cairns.

done.text: She lays a stone on every cairn, one for each name, and the last one on the stone in the middle.
Under the last stone she buries the shard, and doesn't look at it again.
There. They're home.

lines.text: Nell walks the ring of cairns and says a name at each, then many names at each.
And the guilty. I counted the grey coats on the stair, and I heard one name they called. Corin.

steps.objective: Stand with Nell at the cairns.

people.nell: On her people's old winter grounds she laid their names to rest. Corin's name is on her list of the guilty.

story: At the cairns Nell said every name, and then the names of the guilty. Corin's is one of them.

road.text: The wind turns and brings smoke with it, thick and bitter. Something big is burning, far off.

done.text: A house of grey stone, roofless and black. The ash in it is still warm.

lines.text: The wind still smells of smoke. It comes from ahead.

steps.objective: Walk towards the smoke.
story: The wind brought smoke. I followed it to a house of grey stone that had burned.

clues.text: An old man in a grey robe lies across the doorway, his chest opened like the dead of Tollbridge. There is ink on his fingers.
A book on a lectern the fire didn't reach. The letters are like nothing you know: the marks that crawl over an enchanting table.
Footprints in the ash, one person's, small and fresh. They go down the stair.

done.text: A voice comes up the stair, thin and shaking: "Stay where you are. I have a knife."

steps.objective: Look through the burnt house: {found}/{needed}.
story: In the burnt house an old man lay dead at the door, his chest opened. A book on a lectern was written in letters I couldn't read, and fresh footprints went down a stair.

choices.reply: He was old. He'd have hated dying anywhere but at that door.
Wayfarers who stopped walking on purpose, to guard the frames out past the edge of every map. I've never seen one but him.
That one? Everything. Sit down, I'll read it to you.

lines.text: A young woman in a grey robe comes up out of the dark, an armful of books against her chest and a little knife held the wrong way round.
She sees the ember in your hand, and the knife goes down.
A lit ember. Master Ansel waited sixty years for someone to carry one through that door.
I'm Ilse. I was his apprentice. This was the Keepers' reading-house.
Wayfarers came here to learn the oath, in the old script, in the old days. None came in his lifetime.
Three nights ago the night came for it. He sent me down to the vault with the oldest books, and he held the door.

steps.objective: Hear out the woman on the stair.

people.ilse: Ilse, a Keeper's apprentice. Her master died holding the door of their reading-house. She reads the old script.

ilse: Give me a moment. I haven't talked to anyone in three days.

story: Up the stair came Ilse, a Keeper's apprentice, with an armful of books. Her master, Ansel, died holding the door of their reading-house three nights ago.

words.keepers: Wayfarers who stopped walking on purpose, to guard the frames out past the edge of every map. They write everything down.
words.old_script: The writing of the first Wayfarers. Only the Keepers read it now. Its letters are the marks on an enchanting table.

choices.reply: He's dead, and he talks to you. ...Master Ansel would have had a page on that. I'll look.
choices.story: I told Ilse the man whose ember I carry talks to me.
choices.text: The man whose ember I carry.

choices.reply: ...All right.
choices.story: I told Ilse I was listening to nobody.

lines.text: She sits on the top step with the scorched book open on her knees, and reads the marks aloud.
"The Eye sat in the portal between the worlds, and through it the dragon watched everything that stood still. Where it looked, its creatures came."
"Those who lived tore the Eye out, and the dragon went blind. Fire, the sea and the hammer could only break it."
"So they broke it in twelve, and sent each shard to a people at the far ends of the world. Those who carried its light walked."
"Never settle, never shine, everything carried." The oath. He made me copy it every morning.
And the last line, in his hand: "A frame takes whatever of the Eye it is brought. One shard or twelve, it closes the same."
All twelve, or none of this matters.
Ilse looks up from the page. She heard nothing.
Who were you listening to?

steps.objective: Listen to Ilse read.
story: Ilse read me the Keepers' book: the dragon's Eye, torn out and broken in twelve, and the oath. Its last line says a frame takes whatever of the Eye it is brought. The voice said all twelve, or none of this matters.

lines.text: He guarded these his whole life and never saw a single place they talk about.
Take me with you. I can carry books, and I can read them.
She doesn't wait for an answer. She's already packing books into her satchel.

steps.objective: Talk to Ilse.
story: Ilse joined us, with as many of the Keepers' books as she could carry.

lines.text: Go on to your people. I'll bury him first. I know where he wanted to lie.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

lines.text: A Keeper's girl. My grandmother said the Keepers were a story for children.
So did mine. Then she sent me to them.
Can you read me one? Any one. I don't mind which.
Sit down, then. Not that one. That one's sad.

steps.objective: Sit with Tamsin at the caravan's fire.
story: Ilse came in to the caravan's fire at dusk, and Pip had her reading before she'd sat down.

done.text: Low walls in the grass, in a ring round an empty green. Black beams half sunk in the turf. In the middle, an old well.

lines.text: The ember tugs again, out over open grass.

At the far end the stone stands empty.

lines.text: The well is dry. A ladder goes down it, into the dark.

story: The old well was dry. A ladder went down it to a hall with an empty stone.

done.text: So that's where it went.
Her bell. Get it out of there.
Tamsin's bell. All those years it rang over Tollbridge with the shard inside it, and the town under it grew bright enough to burn.

lines.text: The ember warms as you near the stone, the way it did in the Frost Walkers' hall.

steps.objective: Touch the empty stone: right-click it.

people.stranger: Young, he dropped a shard into the first bell of a river crossing, to hide it. The crossing became Tollbridge.
people.tamsin: The shard of the hall under the old green is in her bell. It rang over Tollbridge for forty-five summers, until the night it burned.

story: I touched the stone and woke forty-five summers ago, as him, young. People from a river crossing were casting a bell on the green, and he dropped the shard into their bronze.
It was Tamsin's bell. The shard rang over Tollbridge all those years, until the night it burned.

words.first_village: Wayfarers who swore to stay one winter, and stayed a hundred. Their village burned so long ago the grass has forgotten. Under its well lies their hall.

done.text: The last of the light goes out over the hills, red as a forge.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

steps.awake: Not tonight. The moon is red.
steps.failed: They reach the bell. Tamsin falls, and everything goes dark.

lines.text: The moon comes up over the camp, and it is red.
On its cart, Tamsin's bell hums, though nobody has touched it.
Listen to it. It's never done that.
To the cart, all of you. Something's coming for it.

steps.objective: Hold the camp until morning. Keep them off the bell.

hob: They want the cart. Stand by the cart.
I've got this side. Watch yours.
tamsin: It's calling them. Listen to it.

story: That night the moon came up red, and things came out of the dark for the bell. We held the camp until morning.

done.text: The last of them falls back into the dark. The sky greys, and the red goes out of the moon.
What is left of them crumbles in the sun.

steps.objective: Hold the camp until morning. Keep them off the bell.

hob: The cart's whole. So are we.
tamsin: Not now. Let me sit with it.

asking.text: It's still ringing in my head. Tell me what's in it.
You tell her: the hall under the old green, the casting fire, the hand that dropped the shard into the bronze.
I was nine when they hung it. I carried charcoal for that fire.
It rang for every child born in Tollbridge since. It rang for Pip.
Melt it. Every night it rings, they'll hear it.

choices.reply: Then melt it. Hob. ...Hob, I said melt it.
choices.story: We melted Tamsin's bell and took the shard out of the bronze. She hasn't looked at me since.
choices.text: Melt it. Get the shard out.

choices.reply: It stays. Let it ring for the ones we've got left.
choices.story: Tamsin's bell stays on its cart, with the shard in it.

steps.objective: Tell Tamsin what's in her bell, then decide: press an answer's number.
story: At dawn I told Tamsin what is in her bell. She was nine when they hung it.

lines.text: Hob fires the forge without a word. By noon the bell is a puddle of bronze, and the shard lies in it, cooling.
The shard sinks into the ember. A warmth spreads out from your chest, like standing close to a fire.
Tamsin watches the bronze run. Then she turns her back on you.
She won't forgive you. She's alive not to.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: Since the bell's shard the ember warms me like a fire.

words.warmth: Since the bell's shard the ember warms me like a fire. The cold bites slower.

done.text: As the camp goes up, Tamsin rings her bell, once. All night nothing comes near the fire.

lines.text: Tamsin puts her hand on the bell and leaves it there a long time.
Soft. Every night it rings, they'll hear it.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: Tamsin rings her bell each evening as the camp goes up. Nothing comes near the fire while it rings.

steps.awake: Not yet. Sit by the fire a while.

choices.reply: Because you walk like him now. You should know whose fire it is.
choices.story: I asked her why she told us now. Because I walk like him now, she said.

choices.reply: To see what you do when you know.
choices.story: I asked her what she wants. To see what I do now that I know, she said.
choices.text: What do you want from us?

choices.story: She still wouldn't give her own name. He taught her that, she said.

done.text: It's true. Captain Wend. I served under him six winters.
I never said it. It's not a name you say twice.
Now you know whose fire you carry. Walk well with it.
The fire gusts. Smoke rolls over the circle, and when it thins she is gone.
So now you know my name.
It doesn't change what's in your chest. The rest of them lie past the sea.

lines.text: Someone walks out of the dark and sits down across the fire. The grey hood. The eye stitched over the heart.
At the edge of the light, Corin gets to his feet.
You found his bell. Then you've walked far enough to hear his name.
His name was Wend. A Wayfarer once, and then ours: a captain of the heir's finders.
He raised me.

steps.objective: Sit at the caravan's fire.

people.maren: She told us his name. He raised her. She still won't give her own.
people.stranger: His name was Wend. A Wayfarer once, then a captain of the Gazebound's finders. He raised the hooded woman.

story: The hooded woman came back to our fire and told us his name: Wend. A Wayfarer once, then a captain of the Gazebound's finders. He raised her. Corin says it's true.

steps.objective: Sleep in your tent by the fire.

corin: Six winters. Don't ask me about them tonight.

lines.text: Well? Where does that ember of yours want us now?
You hold it up. It pulls towards the coast, and on past it.
Past the sea. Then we need boats.
I can build a hull. I've never built one that floats.

steps.objective: Talk to Tamsin.
story: At dawn the ember pulled towards the coast, and past it. Tamsin says we need boats.

quests.summary: The hooded woman is somewhere in your smoke again. Sit at the caravan's fire tonight.
quests.title: The Name

done.text: A yard on the shore. A hull on the slip, half planked, and the tar gone cold in its pot.

lines.text: The ember pulls towards the coast. The wind begins to taste of salt.

steps.objective: Follow the pull down to the coast.
story: The ember pulled us down to the coast, to a shipwright's yard with a half-built hull on its slip.

choices.reply: Then you need somebody braver than me. Go and look.
choices.story: I told Edda we need boats for all of us.
choices.text: We need boats for all of us.

choices.reply: The sea happened. Go and look.
choices.story: I asked Edda what happened to him.

lines.text: Don't touch it. It's not for sailing.
A woman with a mallet steps round the hull. Her sleeves are rolled to the elbow and her apron is black with tar.
Edda. The last shipwright on this coast. Nobody wants a boat that goes anywhere.
Nobody crosses that water. My man tried, three summers back.
What's left of his boat lies on the beach, a little way along. Go and look at it. Then tell me you want to cross.

steps.objective: Talk to the woman at the hull.

people.edda: Edda, the last shipwright on the coast. Her husband tried to cross the sea three summers ago. His wreck lies on the beach.

edda: Go and look at it first.
Along the shore. You can't miss it.

story: Edda, the last shipwright on the coast, builds no boats for crossing. Her husband tried it three summers ago. She sent us to look at his wreck.

clues.text: The keel is bitten clean through below the waterline. The marks are a jaw's, and the jaw was wider than your arm is long.
His tool chest, wedged under the ribs. Burned into the lid is the mark you saw on Edda's mallet.
His log, wrapped in oilcloth and still dry. Near the end: "Day 9. Land. A bay where they fish by night and nothing comes for them."

done.text: You wrap the log again. Edda should read the end of it.

steps.objective: Search the wreck on the beach: {found}/{needed}.
story: On the beach lay her husband's boat, its keel bitten through by something with a jaw wider than my arm is long. His log says he made land across the sea, at a bay where they fish by night.

lines.text: Edda takes the log in both hands and reads it standing, to the last page. Then she reads the last page again.
Nine days. He made it across in nine days.
It was coming home that killed him. Coming home to me.
...All right. Bring me timber and I'll build you boats. Thirty-two good logs, any wood.

steps.objective: Take the log back to Edda at the yard.

people.edda: Edda, the last shipwright on the coast. Her husband crossed the sea three summers ago and drowned on the way home. She'll build our boats from timber we bring.

edda: Thirty-two logs. Any wood that floats.
I'll start the moment you bring it.

story: Edda read her husband's log to the end. He made it across in nine days and drowned coming home. She'll build us boats if we bring her timber.

done.text: Good wood. Go to your people. I'll work through the night.

steps.objective: Bring Edda thirty-two logs of any wood and hold them out to her: {carried}/{count}.
steps.short: That's not thirty-two. Hulls don't build from good intentions.
story: We brought Edda timber for the boats. She's working through the night.

lines.text: Go on. Hammering's no music to sleep by.

steps.objective: Make for the caravan's smoke.

hob: A shipwright! I'm going down at first light to watch her work.

steps.objective: Sleep. Edda works through the night.

tamsin: Boats. Forty-five summers on the river, and now boats.

lines.text: The hull on the slip is planked to the gunwale and tarred black. Edda sits at the end of the jetty with her eyes shut.
Every hull I had on the stocks, finished in a night. Take one each.
They'll float and they'll hold, if you don't ask more of them than they can give.
If you find his bay, tell them a shipwright sent you.
There's a valley past the sea where nothing comes at night. I've seen it. Bring them.

steps.objective: Go down to Edda's jetty.

people.edda: Edda, the last shipwright on the coast. She built our boats in a night. If we find her husband's bay, we're to tell them a shipwright sent us.

edda: Mind the tide. And mind what lives under it.

reward.claimed: You walk her round to the jetty. She sits low and steady in the water.

items.name: Edda's Cog

reward.text: a ship of your own, built in a night on Edda's slip.

story: By morning Edda had built our boats. The voice says there's a valley past the sea where nothing comes at night, and that it has seen it.

lines.text: So. Your dead man says there's a valley past the sea where nothing comes at night.
Ask him again how far.
You hold up the ember. It pulls out over the water, and keeps on pulling.
Far enough that nothing follows. Go at dusk.
Dusk. Edda says a night and a day for our tubs, and nobody lands on a strange shore in the dark.
We load today. Tonight we camp on the shore, and then we go.

steps.objective: Talk to Tamsin at Edda's yard.

tamsin: A night and a day. I've done longer on a river barge.

story: Tamsin came down to Edda's yard and asked the voice how far. Far enough that nothing follows, it said, and to go at dusk.

steps.objective: Make for the caravan's smoke. Tonight it camps by the shore.

lines.text: Loaded. Hob wanted to caulk them himself, and Edda threw him off her jetty.
She was right to.
You lead. We'll keep your light in sight, and our lamps hooded.

steps.objective: Sit with Tamsin at the fire.

pip: Is it far? Is it farther than the river?

story: The caravan loaded the boats. We go tonight, with my light in front.

done.text: The coast falls away behind you. Ahead there is only dark water.
Behind you the caravan's boats put out one by one, lamps hooded, following your light.

steps.objective: Put to sea in your ship and sail for open water.
story: We put to sea at night, the caravan's boats behind my light.

held.text: The sky greys. Something long slides away under the boats and doesn't come back.

lines.text: A boat comes up alongside you out of the dark: Tamsin's, with Pip in the bow.
Something knocks against her hull. Then again.
What is that? What's under us?

steps.listing: Tamsin's boat sits low in the water.
steps.objective: Keep Tamsin's boat afloat until morning.
story: Out on the open water something came up from below for Tamsin's boat, and pale dead things climbed out of the sea.

sunk.text: Tamsin's boat rolls over and goes down. Hands haul her and Pip out of the black water into the next boat.
The sky greys. Something long slides away under the boats and doesn't come back.

done.text: Land. A strange coast, and beyond it hills nobody you know has ever walked.

steps.objective: Sail on to the far shore.
story: At first light we sighted land across the sea.

steps.objective: Make for the caravan's smoke, somewhere on this shore.

lines.text: Pip says you beat it off with a lamp and a stick. I had my eyes shut.
It looked at me. It had an eye like a cartwheel.
We lost my boat and everything in it. Not Pip. Not me. Everything else.
The pots, the blankets, half the salt. We'll manage. We've managed with less.
A night and a day, she said. It was one night, and it was long enough.

steps.objective: Sit with Tamsin at the fire.

people.tamsin: She crossed the sea behind my light, in a boat with Pip in the bow, the night something came up from below.

story: We made our first camp across the sea.

done.text: Huts on stilts above the tideline, boats turned keel up on the sand. The village sleeps by day.

lines.text: The ember tugs along the shore, towards something it knows.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: Across the sea the ember pulled along the coast to a village on stilts, and its wardens bowed to me. Nobody told them to.

choices.reply: ...The man in the patched boat. He ate with us and wouldn't stay. He's dead, then. I'm sorry.
choices.story: I told Morwen a shipwright sent us. She remembered Edda's husband.

choices.reply: I hoped you'd tell me.
choices.story: I asked Morwen why the wardens bowed. She hoped I would know.

choices.reply: There's no valley. There's sea, and more sea, and then the cold.
choices.story: I asked Morwen about the valley past the sea. There's no valley, she says. Only sea, and then the cold.
choices.text: We're looking for a valley past the sea.

lines.text: They've never bowed to anyone. Not to me. Not to my mother.
She looks from the wardens to the ember in your hand, and back.
Morwen. I keep this bay, as my mother did.
My grandmother told of people who carried a fire in their hand. Wayfarers. She said one would come for what's under the fire pit.
We're the Tide Folk, what's left of us. Nothing comes up out of this bay at night, so our boats go out with lamps lit, and we eat.
Under the fire pit lies our stone, and on it two shards: ours, and the Drowned City's. Their last people swam it here and made us swear to keep it from the eye.

steps.objective: Talk to the woman with the net.

people.morwen: Morwen keeps the Tide Folk's bay, as her mother did. Under their fire pit lie two shards, theirs and the Drowned City's, and they keep the bay safe at night.

story: Morwen keeps the Tide Folk's bay. Nothing comes up out of it at night, because of two shards under their fire pit: theirs, and the Drowned City's, sworn into their keeping.

words.drowned_city: A city on the coast, the most beautiful in the world, until the sea took it. Its last people swam their shard to the Tide Folk and made them swear to keep it.
words.tide_folk: The people of a bay across the sea. Nothing comes up out of their bay at night, so they fish by lamplight.

done.text: Two shards lie side by side on the dais, one on a stone of its own.

lines.text: They bowed. I've no right to keep you out of anything.
Come down under the fire pit, and see what you'd be taking.

steps.objective: Follow Morwen down under the fire pit.
story: Morwen took me down under the fire pit into the Tide Folk's hall, where two shards lie side by side.

asking.text: Both. They've had their share of safe nights.
Ours keeps the eye off our boats. Theirs keeps the deep things out of the bay.
Take one, and we fish close in, and go hungry. Take both, and we don't fish at all.

choices.reply: Morwen watches you lift them. She doesn't say anything at all.
choices.story: I took both shards. Morwen didn't say anything at all.

choices.reply: ...Close in, then. We'll manage. We'll be thin.
choices.story: I took the Tide Folk's own shard. They'll fish close in, and go hungry.

choices.reply: Then the deep things come back. We'll pull the boats up before dark.
choices.story: I took the Drowned City's shard, and broke the oath they swore. The deep things will come back into the bay.

choices.reply: Morwen lets out a breath she's been holding since the beach.
choices.story: I left both shards on the Tide Folk's stone.

Two at once. You're learning.
