quests.title: The Bay

done.text: A hall cut into the red rock. Its stone stands empty.

lines.text: The ember tugs inland, towards red rock and heat.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The ember pulled inland across the sea's far shore, to a hall in the red canyons, its stone empty.

done.text: The Drowned City's shard. Its last people carried it to the Tide Folk's bay.

steps.objective: Touch the empty stone: right-click it.

seen.text: The ember warms. Three pale figures stand where you stand, and one lifts the shard from the stone into a net.
They climb out of the hall towards the sea. One of them looks back at the stone.

story: The empty stone showed me its last people, pale as foam, lifting the shard into a net and carrying it out towards the sea. It is the second shard on the Tide Folk's stone.

words.drowned_city: Their hall stands in the red canyons, its stone empty. Their last people carried the shard from it to the Tide Folk's bay, the one place on the coast the eye could not see.

lines.text: We have it already. Don't get sentimental about a stone.
We have it already. Don't get sentimental about a stone.
It's in the bay. You know where.
It's in the bay. You know where.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

quests.summary: The ember pulls inland, towards red canyons and heat. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way. Cross them by night, or in shade.
quests.title: The Red Canyons

done.text: Not a camp any more. A lean-to grown into a hut, a chair worn smooth by the fire, a plot dug in rows where something was planted, long dead.

lines.text: There's a camp of mine near here. The last one.
You should see it before you hear about it from someone else.

steps.objective: Find his last camp.
story: The voice sent me to its last camp: a lean-to grown into a hut, and a garden, long dead.

clues.text: A journal on the chair, the ink gone brown. The last page: "Tomorrow I will walk on. I wrote that yesterday too."
On the hearthstone, cut deep and old: an open eye.

steps.objective: Look round his last camp: {found}/{needed}.
story: On the chair lay his journal. Its last page says he'll walk on tomorrow, and that he wrote that yesterday too.

lines.text: The ember warms as you near the hearthstone, the way it did at his first camp.

steps.objective: Touch the hearthstone: right-click it.

people.maren_child: A girl in grey, a tiny eye stitched on her coat. Thirty winters ago she held out the bread he took.

story: I touched the hearthstone and woke thirty winters ago, as him, old and tired. Men in grey sat at his fire, kind, and a girl in grey held out a loaf. He took it. In the morning he wrote that he would walk on tomorrow, and never did.

lines.text: The ember is small for a breath. Then it isn't.
...Enough of that. Walk.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

quests.summary: The voice wants you to see a camp of its, the last one, before you hear about it from someone else.
quests.title: His Last Camp

done.text: Long tents of striped cloth, camels, a fire of thorn. Somebody is singing.

lines.text: The ember tugs into the desert, towards something it can't quite find.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The ember pulled into the desert, to a camp of singers.

choices.reply: Then you need it dead, and we need it alive.
choices.story: I told Sefa we need what the worm swallowed.

choices.reply: Then his song is yours. You'll hear it on its ground.
choices.story: I told Sefa the man who ran was mine.
choices.text: The man who ran was mine.

choices.reply: Then sit, and eat, and go with the shade on your heads.
choices.story: I told Sefa we'd leave the worm be.

done.text: Take the shade. Your heads will thank me.
And this. Blow it on its ground, and it comes up to see who sings. Its eye is where it can be hurt.

lines.text: ...and the sand lay down, and the sand lay still, and the worm went under the hill.
Sefa. I sing for my people, the Sand Singers.
Under the dunes is our hall. One summer the deep sand opened, and something came up and swallowed our stone whole.
It grew. It sees. Nothing on two legs crosses its ground, so no raider has troubled us since.
A man with a coal in his hand fought it once, and ran. His song is the funniest we have.

steps.objective: Listen to the singing woman.

people.sefa: Sefa sings for the Sand Singers. A great worm swallowed their stone and keeps raiders off their ground; they sing to it, and it lets them be.

reward.claimed: You pull the shade over your head. The sun lets go of you.

items.name: Sand Singers' Hood
items.tooltip: Woven from palm and reed. Keeps the sun off your head.

items.name: Sand Singers' Shade
items.tooltip: Woven from palm and reed. Keeps the sun off your back.

items.name: The Sand Singers' Horn
items.tooltip: Blow it on the worm's ground, and it comes up to see who sings.

reward.text: the Sand Singers' shade, woven from palm and reed, and a horn that sings.
reward.title: The Shade and the Horn

story: Sefa sings for the Sand Singers. A great worm swallowed the stone in their hall, and grew, and sees, and keeps the raiders away. A man with a coal in his hand once fought it, and ran.

words.sand_singers: Nomads of the desert. They dug a hall under the dunes, and sing to the worm that swallowed its stone.
words.worm: A great worm that came up out of the deep sand and swallowed the Sand Singers' stone. It grew, and it sees.

done.text: A bowl of sand ringed with old bones. In the middle, a broken spear.

lines.text: Its ground is that way. A morning's walk. Walk softly.

steps.objective: Find the worm's ground.
story: Its ground is a bowl of sand ringed with old bones, and in the middle lies a broken spear.

lines.text: The ember warms as you near the spear.

steps.objective: Touch the broken spear: right-click it.
story: The spear was his. When I touched it I was him, thirty-five winters ago, and the worm came up out of the dune with an eye as big as a door, and I ran. Somewhere behind me, the Sand Singers laughed.

killed.text: The worm shudders and sinks into the sand, and does not come up. Where it lay, something hums.

lines.text: Blow it. It's only a worm.

steps.objective: Blow the horn on its ground and fight it, or walk away and leave it be.

rises.text: The sand heaves. An eye opens in the dune, as big as a door, and looks at whoever sang.

spared.text: You leave the bowl behind. The sand lies still.

story: At the bowl the voice wanted the horn blown. It's only a worm, it said.

lines.text: The shard sinks into the ember. Far off, the horizon sharpens, as if you could reach out and touch it.
And a worm. You're better at this than he was.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: I killed the worm, and took the shard out of it. Far places show sharp through a spyglass now. The Sand Singers have no protector.

words.far_sight: Since the worm's shard far places show sharp through a spyglass.

lines.text: It's a worm. You left a shard in a worm.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: I left the worm alive, and the shard in it. The Sand Singers keep their protector.

quests.summary: The ember pulls into the desert, towards a stone it can't quite find. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: The Singers

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

choices.reply: Shine. Like a cat's, but the wrong colour.
choices.story: I asked Corin what my eyes do. Shine, he said, like a cat's, but the wrong colour.

choices.reply: ...Yes. It's the fire.
choices.story: I told them it's the fire. Agna agreed too quickly.

choices.reply: Then you know more than us.
choices.story: I told them I know. Corin said I know more than them, then.

done.text: It's the fire, Corin. Everyone's eyes do that.
Agna looks for herself. She stops laughing.
Leave it. All of you.
Firelight. Sit down.

lines.text: Across the fire Corin is looking at you, and keeps looking.
Corin. What are you staring at?
Your eyes. Did you know they do that?

steps.objective: Sit with them at the fire.

people.corin: He saw my eyes catch the firelight like an animal's, pale, the wrong colour. Agna saw it too, and stopped laughing.

story: At the fire Corin saw my eyes shine in the firelight, pale, like an animal's but the wrong colour. Agna laughed, and then she looked, and stopped.

quests.summary: Corin has been watching you across the fire for days. Sit with them tonight.
quests.title: Your Eyes

done.text: A long, low house of mossy stone at the head of a stair, its door open. Bars inside it, one behind the other.
In the mud by the door, boot prints, days old. Grey cloth caught on a thorn.

lines.text: The ember tugs into the green, towards something locked.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The ember pulled into the jungle, to a lock house of mossy stone at the head of the Jungle Folk's stair. Someone in grey came this way days ago.

done.text: The last bars grind up into the stone. Far down, under your feet, something old wakes and hums.
And through the ground, plain as day, as if the rock were smoke: three men by a stone, one with maps open on the dais.

lines.text: Four levers on the wall, and over them four stones. Two of them catch the ember's light.

steps.objective: Open the Jungle Folk's locks: three doors of bars.

opens.text: Bars grind up into the stone. The next door waits.

story: Three locks kept the Jungle Folk's stone asleep: levers under marked stones, their word written on a sign, and two plates held down at once. When the last bars rose I saw through the ground, as if the rock were smoke, three men waiting by the stone below.

words.jungle_folk: They built locks that never slept, and the eye never found the way in. It found them instead, one by one.
words.stone_sight: Since the Jungle Folk's locks I see through stone: standing still at night, the night's creatures show through the rock.

choices.reply: That someone watches. Someone always watched. I'd only make it kind.
choices.story: I asked him the price. Someone watches, he said; someone always did. He'd only make it kind.

choices.reply: He served my father. He thought he was clever. Then he stopped walking.
choices.story: I told him Wend served them. He served his father, he said, and then stopped walking.

choices.reply: Gladly. I've stood here long enough.
choices.story: I told him to get out of my way.

done.text: Lift it. I'll take it from you at the gate.

lines.text: He doesn't turn. His men do.
The Grass King's son, since you're too polite to ask. I've been here four days. It won't lift for me.
Only an ember wakes a stone. He knew that. It's all in his maps.
I want a world where everything is seen, and nothing hides in the dark. No thieves. No war. Nobody needs a tent in a world like that.

steps.objective: Go down to the stone. Someone is waiting there.

people.heir: The Grass King's son. He waited four days at the Jungle Folk's stone with Wend's maps, and couldn't lift the shard: only an ember wakes a stone. He wants a world where everything is seen.

story: The Grass King's son waited at the Jungle Folk's stone with Wend's old maps. It wouldn't lift for him. He wants a world where everything is seen, where nobody needs a tent.

words.heir: The Grass King's son. He leads the Gazebound now, and he has Wend's maps of the halls.

asking.text: Take it. Let him try at the gate.
Go on. I won't touch you here. Not yet.

choices.reply: He folds his maps. "At the gate, then." His men follow him up the stair.
choices.story: I took the Jungle Folk's shard. The heir folded his maps and said he'd see me at the gate.

choices.reply: He looks at you a long time. "Then it sleeps here, and we both come back for it." His men follow him up the stair.
choices.story: I left the Jungle Folk's shard asleep on their stone. The heir said we'd both come back for it.

steps.objective: Decide what you take from their stone.
story: On the Jungle Folk's stone lay their shard, and the Grass King's son stood by to watch me lift it.

lines.text: The shard sinks into the ember.
He's right about one thing. Someone always watched.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: I carry the Jungle Folk's shard. The voice says the heir is right about one thing: someone always watched.

lines.text: You left it for him to sit beside. He's patient. So am I.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: I left the Jungle Folk's shard asleep. The voice says it is patient.

quests.summary: The ember pulls into the jungle, to the Jungle Folk's hall. Someone in grey went that way days ago. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: The Locks

steps.awake: Not yet. Sit by the fire a while.

choices.reply: I can't. I swore. Look at what he wants, not what he says.
choices.story: I asked her where he's leading us. She couldn't say: she swore. Look at what he wants, she said, not what he says.

choices.reply: You know who. You carry him.
choices.story: I asked her who she meant. You carry him, she said.

choices.reply: He raised me. I owe him that much, and you more.
choices.story: I asked her why she'd tell me. He raised her, she said; she owes him that much, and me more.

done.text: She stands. The fire gusts, smoke rolls over the circle, and when it thins she is gone.
Somewhere in the ember, something laughs, low and long, and doesn't stop for a while. It doesn't sound like a man.

lines.text: The grey hood comes out of the dark again, and sits down across the fire. Her hands are empty.
No bread tonight?
Not tonight.
He isn't leading you where you think.

steps.objective: Sit at the caravan's fire.

people.maren: She came to our fire again without bread, and warned me: he isn't leading us where we think.

story: The hooded woman came to our fire again, without bread, and warned me that he isn't leading us where I think. When she was gone the voice laughed, and it didn't sound like a man.

quests.summary: Someone walked in your smoke again today. Sit at the caravan's fire tonight.
quests.title: The Hooded Woman's Warning

road.text: We're close. Camp in the hollow tonight, out of the wind.

done.text: The last of the light goes out over the hills, red as a forge.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

lines.text: This is it. The valley.
This is it? This is his valley?
Grass, a stream, low hills on every side. Out of the wind.
Hob laughs, for the first time in weeks.

steps.objective: Sit with them at the fire.
story: The voice brought us to a hollow among low hills and called it the valley. Hob laughed for the first time in weeks.

steps.awake: Not tonight. The moon is red.

lines.text: The moon comes up over the hollow, and it is red.
On every hill around the camp, something stands up out of the grass.
Everyone to the fire. Everyone.

steps.objective: Hold on until morning. It can't be won, only lived through.

hob: They're in the tents. Get them out of the tents!
tamsin: To the fire! Stay in the light!

story: That night the moon came up red over the hollow, and the gaze came down on us from every hill. Tents caught. People ran.

done.text: The sky greys. The red goes out of the moon, and the last of them crumbles in the light.
The fires are out. Nine wagons are gone.
Tamsin went back into the burning tents for the others, and didn't come out.
Hob held the wagons' line with a cracked hammer until it broke, and then a while longer.
Agna lies by the healers' tent, a remedy she never learned unmixed in her hands.
Pip ran on foot, and was too slow.
Corin's tent is empty. Grey coats took him alive; his old company wanted him back.
Ilse's book tent is ash. She was in it, reading.
Nell's shelter is empty. She went into the hills before dawn, without a word.
Don't cry. You'll need the water.
I needed you alone.

steps.objective: Hold on until morning.
story: By dawn the fires were out and nine wagons were gone.
Over the ashes the voice spoke, and it wasn't his voice any more: I needed you alone. Whatever is in the ember, it was never Wend.

words.the_gaze: Whatever speaks from the ember: the gaze itself. It used Wend's voice until the night at the hollow. It needed me alone.

quests.summary: The voice says the valley is close, and wants the caravan to camp in the hollow tonight.
quests.title: The Hollow

clues.text: A potter, one arm burned to the elbow. You carry him to the wagons.
A girl from the last wagon, her ankle twisted under her. She doesn't cry until you put her down.
An old drover who won't stop shaking. You sit him on a sack of flour and he holds your sleeve.

done.text: Whoever is left of the wagons takes them from you at the cart's tail, and nobody says thank you, and nobody needs to.

steps.objective: Carry the wounded to the wagons, with the ember held up to find them: {found}/{needed}.
story: At dawn I carried the wounded out of the ash to the wagons.

clues.text: You close the first grave. The earth is still warm from the fires.
The second. Someone has put a wooden spoon on it.
The third, the smallest.

done.text: Three mounds where the tents stood, one for each lost household. Nobody marks them. Nobody wants the night to find them again.

steps.objective: Close the graves where the tents stood: {found}/{needed}.
story: We buried the dead of the hollow in three graves where the tents had stood.

lines.text: Those who are left load what is left. Nobody asks where. When you walk, they follow.
I have no voice. I never needed one. I only looked.
His is the only one I have. I'm sorry it's his.

steps.objective: Listen.
story: Those who are left followed me out of the hollow. The gaze spoke openly for the first time: it has no voice of its own, only his.

quests.summary: The hollow at dawn. The wounded need carrying to the wagons, and the dead need graves.
quests.title: The Morning After

done.text: A mast on the high ground, a hut, a rack of grey robes. Moored to the mast, something with a gasbag the size of a barn.

lines.text: They fly from a field on the high ground. Wear their grey and they'll take you for one of theirs.

steps.objective: Find the Gazebound's airfield on the high ground.
story: The Gazebound fly from a field on the high ground, with a mast and a moored airship.

clues.text: Grey robes, an open eye stitched on each. One of them is your size.

steps.objective: Take a grey robe from the rack.

reward.claimed: You pull the grey over your head. It smells of other people's fires.

items.name: Gazebound Robe
items.tooltip: Grey, with an open eye on the breast. Their kind won't turn on you in it, unless you strike first.

reward.text: a grey robe with an open eye on the breast.
reward.title: Their Grey

story: I took a grey robe from the Gazebound's rack. In it, their kind take me for one of their own.

lines.text: Up. Look down. Tell me what you see.

steps.objective: Board the airship.
story: I boarded the Gazebound's airship. The sky is open now: airships and gliders lift for us.

lines.text: From up here the caravan's smoke is a grey thread, and the world is very small.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke, by air if you like.

quests.summary: The gaze says the Gazebound fly from a field on the high ground, and that their grey would get you aboard.
quests.title: Wings

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

done.text: You wake with a start. In the dream you looked down at the world from very high, and it was very small, and everything in it stood still.
I've nothing for that. I'm sorry.
Nobody says anything. There's nobody left who would know what to say.
That was me. That's what I see. All of it.

steps.objective: Sleep by the fire.
story: I dreamt I looked down at the world from very high, and it was small, and everything in it stood still. The gaze said that was what it sees.

quests.summary: Something is wrong with your sleep. Sit at the fire tonight.
quests.title: The Dreaming

done.text: Walls of sandstone across the stair, a gate of bars, and before them tents with the open eye on their banners.
Wayfarer! Their champion has called out whoever carries the light. Beat him, and we open the gate.

lines.text: The ember tugs out over the grass, towards walls.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The ember pulled to the Grass Kingdom's walls, and the heir's army camped before them.

lines.text: You! The one with the coal! Come and take it off me, if you want the gate.

steps.name: The heir's champion
steps.objective: Beat the heir's champion before the gate.
story: The heir's champion called me out before the Grass Kingdom's gate, and I beat him.

won.text: The champion goes down in the grass. Behind you, the bars grind up.

done.text: Lift it, and the ward falls with it, and they come over the walls tonight. Leave it, and we stand, and we'll remember who left it.

lines.text: We tore it from our king's crown. He saw everything that stood still, for one summer, and it ate him.
Under the seal it keeps the ward round our walls. That's all it does now. It's enough.

steps.objective: Go down to the stone with the warden.

people.warden: The Grass Kingdom's warden. They tore their shard from their king's crown and sealed it under their walls, where it keeps the ward.

story: The warden took me to the stone under their seal, which keeps the ward round the Grass Kingdom's walls.

words.grass_kingdom: The kingdom of the grasslands. Their king wore his people's shard in his crown and saw everything that stood still, for one summer. They tore it from him and sealed it under their walls.

asking.text: Take it. Walls fall. Kingdoms always fall.

choices.reply: Then hold our walls tonight. You owe us that much.
choices.story: I took the Grass Kingdom's shard, and the ward fell.

choices.reply: The kingdom will remember this. So will I.
choices.story: I left the Grass Kingdom's shard under their seal. The kingdom trusts me.

steps.objective: Decide what you take from their stone.
story: Under the Grass Kingdom's seal lay their shard.

lines.text: The ward goes out like a lamp. Over the grass the heir's army stands up, all at once.

steps.objective: Hold the gate against the heir's army.
story: The ward fell, and the heir's army came for the gate, and we held it.

lines.text: The shard sinks into the ember. Above, the things that hunt from the sky lose you, and circle.
He has his ancestors' land back, if he wants it. He'll want it.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: Since the Grass Kingdom's shard the things of the sky don't see me.

words.sky_veil: Since the Grass Kingdom's shard the things that hunt from the sky don't see me.

lines.text: A kingdom that trusts you. How useful. How sweet.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: The Grass Kingdom stands, and trusts me.

quests.summary: The ember pulls towards the Grass Kingdom, its walls and the heir's army camped before them. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: The Ward

done.text: The Shadow Circle's hall. Its stone is empty, and the floor is scuffed with boots.
Grey-coat tracks lead away from the stair, between the trees.

lines.text: The ember tugs into the dark trees.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The ember pulled into the dark forest to the Shadow Circle's hall. Its stone was empty, and grey-coat tracks led away from it.

done.text: A house of dark oak in the shape of the Circle's halls, its windows grey glass. Smoke from the chimney. Nobody at the door.

steps.objective: Follow the tracks to where they lead.
story: The tracks led to a Gazebound house built in the shape of the Shadow Circle's halls.

clues.text: A ledger in his hand. The halls he found for them, one by one, and on the last page: "The girl. Maren. Mine now."

steps.objective: Look round the room upstairs, with the ember held up: {found}/{needed}.
story: Upstairs was his room. His ledger lay on the desk.

lines.text: His chair stands by the cold hearth. The ember warms as you come near it.

steps.objective: Sit in his chair: right-click it.
story: I sat in his chair and woke as him, younger, in this house when it was new. A girl in grey sat by his fire and talked to his ember, because he told her it listens.

asking.text: A horn outside. Boots on the stairs. There's time to get one thing out of this cellar.

choices.reply: You lift the shard and run. Behind you the cage rattles.
choices.story: I took the Shadow Circle's shard, and left the children in the cage.

choices.reply: You break the cage and run with them, out into the trees.
choices.story: I broke the cage and got the children out, and left the shard.

steps.objective: Decide what you get out of the cellar.
story: In the cellar the Shadow Circle's shard sat on a stand, and three children of a burnt town sat in a cage beside it.

lines.text: The shard sinks into the ember. In the dark, what hunts stops noticing you, as long as you walk.
Good. Don't look back.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: Since the Shadow Circle's shard, the night's creatures don't notice me unless I run.

words.night_walk: Since the Shadow Circle's shard, the night's creatures don't notice me at night unless I run.

done.text: The children sleep in a heap by the fire, and the caravan's people take turns to watch them.

lines.text: Three mouths. One shard. You can count, can't you?

steps.objective: Make for their smoke, with the children.
story: I brought three children of a burnt town to the caravan.

quests.summary: The ember pulls into the dark forest, towards a stone it can't quite find. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: The Mansion

done.text: Shelves cut into the mountain, and books on every one. On the stone, the shard hums among them.

lines.text: The ember tugs upwards, into the thin air.

steps.objective: Follow the pull up the mountain.
story: The ember pulled up to the Scribes' hall near a peak, its shelves full of books.

done.text: The book he stopped at speaks of a thirteenth shard. "The one that walks."
Here. These words. They close an Eye. Not break it. Close it.
You can read it yourself: the old script Ilse taught you crawls into words. How an Eye is closed, not broken.

steps.objective: Touch the stone: right-click it.

seen.text: Candlelight. A man in a Wayfarer's coat reads at their lectern, his ember bright, turning pages fast.
He stops at one page, and doesn't turn it for a long time.

story: The stone showed me Wend reading at the Scribes' lectern. He stopped at a page about a thirteenth shard, the one that walks. On it are the words that close an Eye.

words.close_words: The words that close an Eye, from the Scribes' books. Not break it: close it.

asking.text: Take it. Books don't need it.

choices.reply: The books fall silent on their shelves.
choices.story: I took the Scribes' shard.

choices.reply: You leave it humming among the books.
choices.story: I left the Scribes' shard among their books.

steps.objective: Decide what you take from their stone.
story: The Scribes' shard lay on their stone among the books.

lines.text: The shard sinks into the ember. Held up against a blow, it would burst like a lamp.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: Since the Scribes' shard the ember flares when the night strikes at me while I hold it up, and what's near crumbles.

words.flare: Since the Scribes' shard, held up against a blow, the ember bursts and what's near crumbles. It fills again at a fire.

lines.text: You read too much. He did too.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: I left the Scribes' shard.

quests.summary: The ember pulls up into the mountains, towards a hall near a peak. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: The Scribes' Books

done.text: Rows of graves under old pines, each with a circle and a line cut on its stone. Wayfarers, all of them.

lines.text: The ember tugs into the old pines.

steps.objective: Follow the pull: walk where the ember flares.
story: The ember pulled to the Grave Keepers' graveyard, rows of Wayfarers under old pines.

clues.text: One grave is open, and empty, its stone fresh. WEND. Under it, small, cut by another hand: M.

steps.objective: Look round the graves with the ember held up.
story: One grave is open and empty. Its stone says WEND, and under it, small: M.

asking.text: Take it. The dead won't mind. Much.

choices.reply: The ground shivers under the pines.
choices.story: I took the Grave Keepers' shard, and the dead woke.

choices.reply: The dead sleep.
choices.story: I left the Grave Keepers' shard with their dead.

steps.objective: Decide what you take from their stone.
story: The Grave Keepers' shard lay on their stone, among the dead they buried.

steps.awake: Not tonight. The moon is red.

lines.text: The moon comes up over the pines, and it is red.
Between the graves the earth heaves.

steps.objective: Hold the graveyard until morning.
story: That night the moon came up red and the dead woke, and we held the graveyard until morning.

done.text: The sky greys. The dead lie down again, and the red goes out of the moon.

steps.objective: Hold the graveyard until morning.

lines.text: The shard sinks into the ember. When you crouch, its light sinks to nothing, like a dead man's.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: Since the Grave Keepers' shard, when I crouch my light sinks like a dead man's, and the night's creatures lose me.

words.hush: Since the Grave Keepers' shard, when I crouch my light sinks like a dead man's, and the night's creatures lose me.

lines.text: His grave, and you left it full of nothing. She'll be pleased.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: I left the Grave Keepers' shard with their dead.

quests.summary: The ember pulls into old pines, towards a hall among graves. Hold it up, turn until it flares, and walk that way.
quests.title: The Empty Grave

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.

caught.text: You're on him. He drops the child into the grass and wheels the horse.
He doesn't want the child. He wants you at the gate.
Then he's gone into the dark.

lines.text: Hooves out of the dark, a rider in grey, and he's through the fire and away with a child across his saddle.
Help! Help me!

steps.objective: Catch the rider.
story: A rider in grey snatched a child from our fire. I caught him; he said the heir doesn't want the child, he wants me at the gate.

done.text: The child has held your hand all the way back to the fire, and won't let go until morning.

steps.objective: Bring the child back to the fire.

quests.summary: The heir's riders have been seen near the caravan. Sit at the fire tonight, and keep the children close.
quests.title: The Rider

done.text: Down the stronghold's stairs, a hall of the frame, and old people in hoods waiting by it as if they knew you'd come.

lines.text: The frame. Down there. Don't let them talk you out of it.

steps.objective: Go down to the Keepers' frame.
story: The Keepers waited at the frame in the stronghold, as if they knew I'd come.

choices.reply: You. You're what it's been walking towards.
choices.story: I asked the Keeper what it means. Me, she said.

choices.reply: Ask it.
choices.story: I told the Keeper she was lying. Ask it, she said.

done.text: The thirteenth.
...Yes.

lines.text: The oldest of them looks at the ember. Then she looks at your eyes, and doesn't look away.
We barred our door to him, and he gave it to you. Of course he did.
Twelve shards in their halls. And the Eye's last piece walks. A frame takes whatever of the Eye it's brought.

steps.objective: Face the Keepers at the frame.

people.oldest_keeper: The oldest of the Keepers at the frame. She named me: the thirteenth.

story: The oldest Keeper named me the thirteenth: the Eye's last piece, put in me when Wend gave me the ember. A frame takes whatever of the Eye it's brought.

words.thirteenth: The Eye's last piece. It walks: it was put in me with the ember.

quests.summary: The last hall of the far ring is behind you. The Keepers keep the frame in the nearest stronghold. The ember wants it.
quests.title: The Keepers' Door

lines.text: Boots on the stair. The heir's band comes down into the hall of the frame, and the heir with them.
Beside him walks a woman in a grey hood.
...Wait.
She breaks the seal on an old letter, reads it, and turns her staff on the men beside her.

steps.objective: Hold the frame against the heir's band.
story: The heir's band came down into the hall of the frame. We held it.

lines.text: He wrote it the night he gave you the ember. Thirty winters I carried it, and never read it.
Maren. My name's Maren. He'd want you to have it.
The last of them falls back up the stair. The heir is not among the dead.

steps.objective: Listen.
story: The heir's band broke on the stair.

lines.text: Over the frame the ember warms, the way it did at his camps. Something here remembers him.

steps.objective: Touch the frame: right-click it.
story: At the frame the ember showed me Wend's last night: he knew what he gave me. His last words were his own: don't let it look at them.

quests.summary: Boots on the stronghold's stair. The heir has come for the frame, and for you.
quests.title: The Gate

choices.reply: Then set what you carry in the frame, and go through. It'll see only what you give it.
choices.story: I chose to blind it: to set the shards in the frame and fight what's on the other side.

choices.reply: ...So be it. Somewhere, there'll be one place where nothing comes at night.
choices.story: I gave the gaze its sight, for the home it promised.

choices.reply: Then take them back to the peoples who'll hide them, and walk. The road goes on.
choices.story: I kept the oath: the shards go back to the peoples who trust me, and the road goes on.

choices.reply: Then say the words, and step in. It'll be dark. It'll be the first dark it's ever had.
choices.story: I chose to close the Eye.

lines.text: Give me my sight. I'll give you a home where nothing comes at night. I keep my promises.
There it is. The frame takes whatever of the Eye it's brought. Choose.

steps.objective: Choose a door: press its number.
story: At the frame I had to choose what it does with the Eye.

lines.text: You'd blind me. Then come and do it. I can almost see you.

steps.objective: Set the shards in the frame, go through, and blind it.
story: I set the shards in the frame and went through, and fought what looked out of it with the sight I'd given it.

lines.text: It falls. Its eye goes dark for good.
Back in the world, the nights are only nights. Nothing comes. A tent is only a tent.
Far below, in the deep dark, the sculk creeps one block further. Nobody hears it.

steps.objective: Remember.
story: The Eye is blind. The nights are only nights. Build a home.

lines.text: The frame opens like an eye. Everything that stands still, everywhere, is seen at once.
There. Where your people sleep. Nothing will come there at night. I keep my promises.
Everywhere else, the towns start to burn.
Far below, in the deep dark, the sculk creeps one block further. Nobody hears it.

steps.objective: Remember.
story: I gave it its sight. It kept its promise: where my people sleep, nothing comes at night. Everywhere else, it sees.

lines.text: You take the shards back out into the world, one by one, to the peoples who'll hide them again.
Half-blind, then. As I've always been. Walk, little light.
Far below, in the deep dark, the sculk creeps one block further. Nobody hears it.

steps.objective: Remember.
story: I kept the oath. The shards go back to their peoples, and the road goes on.

lines.text: You say the words. The frame goes still, and the light takes you.
For the first time... it's dark. Thank you, little light.
Your friends are alone at the fire.
Pip sits closest to it, a coal in cupped hands. It hasn't gone out.
Far below, in the deep dark, the sculk creeps one block further. Nobody hears it.

steps.objective: Remember.
story: I closed the Eye. For the first time it's dark.

quests.summary: The frame waits. Choose what it does with the Eye.
quests.title: The Doors

lines.text: Wil the cooper. The last of Tollbridge I can't account for.
He went to his sister's village the spring before we burned. Up the valley, he said. Find out if he lived.

steps.objective: Hear Tamsin out at the fire.

people.tamsin: She can't account for one of Tollbridge: Wil the cooper, who went to his sister's village the spring before it burned.

story: Tamsin asked me to find Wil the cooper, the last of Tollbridge she can't account for, in his sister's village.

done.text: Smoke from chimneys. A village, still standing.

steps.objective: Find Wil in his sister's village.
story: Wil's sister's village still stands.

choices.reply: ...Fine. Fine! Let me get my tools.
choices.story: I asked Wil to come with us, and he did.

choices.reply: Thank you. Tell her I'm well. Tell her she owes me a barrel.
choices.story: I let Wil stay in the village.

lines.text: An old man sits by the well, mending a barrel hoop.
Tamsin sent you? Tamsin's alive? Well. Of course she is.
The night's come closer every week. My sister's gone. Let it come. I'm tired of running.

steps.objective: Find Wil in his sister's village.

people.wil: Wil the cooper, the last of Tollbridge. His sister's gone. He's tired of running.

story: Wil the cooper lives, in his sister's village. His sister's gone, and he's tired of running.

done.text: Wil. Sit, you old fool. Sit by me.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: Wil came with us. Tamsin made him sit by her at the fire.

done.text: Wil. Still alive. Still stubborn.
Tamsin laughs, and then she doesn't.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke, and tell Tamsin.
story: Wil stayed in his village. Tamsin laughed, and then she didn't.

quests.summary: Tamsin's last townsman, Wil the cooper, went to his sister's village the spring before Tollbridge burned. Find out if he lived.
quests.title: The Missing

lines.text: The Keepers kept a house on this shore. Sealed. They seal what they won't burn.
The seal takes three words of the oath. You'll see them better than I will, with that thing.

steps.objective: Hear Ilse out at the fire.
story: Ilse told me of a sealed Keepers' house on this shore. The seal takes three words of the oath.

done.text: Broken walls of grey stone, and a door of black stone that was never broken.

steps.objective: Find the Keepers' sealed house.
story: The Keepers' house stands broken, but its sealed door never was.

clues.text: A word cut into the stone, glowing under the ember: WALK.
Another, half under moss: CARRY.
The last, by the door itself: NEVER STAY.

done.text: The black stone of the door sighs, and runs out of its frame like sand.

steps.objective: Find the seal's three words with the ember held up: {found}/{needed}.
story: The seal's three words were cut into the walls round it: walk, carry, never stay. When I found them all, the door ran out of its frame like sand.

steps.objective: Read what the Keepers sealed in.
story: The Keepers sealed in a note: Wend came to their door with his ember small, and asked to stay one winter. They barred the door, and he cursed them and walked off towards the grey coats.

done.text: Now. The old script. Sit.
She teaches you until the fire's low: the marks that crawl over an enchanting table, and what they say.

lines.text: They barred the door to him. And he went to them.
If I die, nobody will be left who can read the Keepers' words. That can't happen.

steps.objective: Bring Ilse what the Keepers sealed in.

people.ilse: She taught me the old script, so it outlives her.

story: Ilse taught me the old script, so that someone can read the Keepers' words if she dies.

words.old_script: The writing of the first Wayfarers. Ilse taught it to me, so it outlives her.

quests.summary: Ilse says the Keepers kept a house on this shore, and sealed it. They seal what they won't burn.
quests.title: The Seal

lines.text: Wren. The potter's girl. It's the marsh fever, the kind I can't break.
The Tide Folk can. If she's in their bay before the third dawn. Take her.

steps.objective: Hear Agna out at the fire.

people.wren: The potter's girl. She burns with the marsh fever.

story: Wren, the potter's girl, burns with the marsh fever. Agna can't break it; the Tide Folk can, before the third dawn.

arrived.text: Wren sits down in the sand and doesn't get up. Morwen comes down the beach at a run.

steps.each: Wren coughs in her sleep. Dawns left: {left}.

late.text: Before the third dawn Wren stops coughing. She's very light to carry back.

lines.text: I'm Wren. I can walk. I'm not tired.

steps.objective: Walk Wren to the Tide Folk's bay before the third dawn.
story: I walked Wren towards the Tide Folk's bay, slowly, with the dawns counting down.

done.text: Morwen writes it down for your healer: bladderwrack, salt, a night in the bay's water.

lines.text: Marsh fever. Give her here.
Bladderwrack and salt, steeped in our water. It breaks the fever, and for a day what looks for you looks past you. We use it on the boats.

steps.objective: Give Wren to Morwen.
story: Morwen took Wren in and broke her fever, and wrote the remedy down for Agna. For a day, whoever drinks it is looked past.

lines.text: Seaweed, salt, and something that hides you. So that's what I was missing.
Wren?
You tell her. Agna sits down very suddenly.

steps.objective: Bring Agna the Tide Folk's remedy.

people.agna: She learned the Tide Folk's remedy, which breaks the marsh fever and hides whoever drinks it for a day.

story: Agna learned the Tide Folk's remedy from Morwen's note. Wren lives.

done.text: ...Give her to me.
Agna sits with Wren until morning, and nobody asks her to stop.

steps.objective: Bring Wren home.
story: Wren died on the road to the bay, before the third dawn. Agna sat with her until morning.

quests.summary: Wren, the potter's girl, burns with a fever Agna can't break. The Tide Folk's healer can, before the third dawn.
quests.title: The Fever

lines.text: The boats go out tonight. Come with them.
The boats go out tonight, and something will see them now. Come with them. Please.

steps.objective: Hear Morwen out at the bay.
story: Morwen asked me to go out with the Tide Folk's boats at night.

lines.text: Lanterns on the black water. Then, from the deep, things climbing up the hulls.
They see us now! Hold them off the boats!

steps.objective: Hold the night off the Tide Folk's boats.
story: The Tide Folk's boats were seen that night, and we held the deep things off them.

lines.text: Lanterns on black water, and nets coming up full. Nothing comes. Somebody sings, badly.
Like it was before. Take some home.

steps.objective: Fish with the Tide Folk.

reward.claimed: You pack the fish. They're still cold from the bay.
reward.text: a share of the night's catch.
reward.title: The Catch

story: I fished with the Tide Folk at night, and nothing came. Like it was before, Morwen said.

quests.summary: Morwen asks if you'll go out with the Tide Folk's boats tonight.
quests.title: Night Fishing

lines.text: Riders on the dunes. Nobody crossed our ground while it lived. Now they do.
Sit with us. We'll sing you its song, now that you've heard it.

steps.objective: Go to the Sand Singers' camp.
story: Sefa sent word from the desert.

lines.text: Torches on the dunes. They come down on the camp from three sides.

steps.objective: Hold the Sand Singers' camp.
story: With the worm dead, raiders came for the Sand Singers, and we held their camp.

lines.text: Sefa sings it: the sand lying down, the worm under the hill, and a man with a coal in his hand, running. Everyone laughs at the same place.
Then they sing it again, and this time the man turns round.

steps.objective: Listen.
story: The Sand Singers sang me the worm's song. The second time, the man with the coal turned round.

quests.summary: Sefa sent word: something's changed in the desert.
quests.title: The Raiders

done.text: Doors barred, shutters nailed. They know what's coming, and they can't walk away from it.

steps.objective: Get to the village before nightfall.
story: The night was coming for a village we traded with.

lines.text: Dusk. Then, in every shadow round the village, something stands up.

steps.objective: Save whom you can.
story: We held the village through the night, and saved whom we could.

done.text: By morning half the roofs are gone. The rest of the village will be a ruin by next spring; you'll pass it.

steps.objective: Hold until morning.

quests.summary: Smoke on the road ahead: a village the caravan traded with. The night is coming for it.
quests.title: The Burning

choices.reply: ...Fine. He sits on the far side. I don't have to look at him.
choices.story: I made them both stay. Corin sits on the far side of the fire now.
choices.text: We need you both. Sit apart, but sit.

choices.reply: Then he goes. Tonight. I won't watch him do it.
choices.story: I sided with Nell. Corin walked into the dark without a word.

choices.reply: Then I'll go. I've buried them. That's all I stayed for.
choices.story: I sided with Corin. Nell went back to the snow.

lines.text: He was on the stair. He was one of them.
I was. I left. I've said it a hundred times.
You left late.

steps.objective: Settle it between Nell and Corin.
story: Nell and Corin couldn't share a fire any more.

quests.summary: Nell and Corin can't share a fire any more. Someone has to settle it.
quests.title: The Quarrel

done.text: In a cottage at the village's edge an old man sits by a cold hearth, a coal in his palm no bigger than a seed.

steps.objective: Follow the ember to the other light.
story: The ember led me to a village where an old Wayfarer settled long ago.

choices.reply: ...One more road, then. One. Don't watch me go, it's embarrassing.
choices.story: I talked Oswin back onto the road. His coal brightened.

choices.reply: Thank you. Sit with me till it's out.
choices.story: I sat with Oswin until his ember went out. Somewhere, the gaze saw a little more.

lines.text: Oswin. I walked for forty years. Then I met a woman with a garden, and I stopped.
She's gone now. The coal's going too. I'm tired.

steps.objective: Talk to the old man by the hearth.

people.settled_wayfarer: Oswin, an old Wayfarer who stopped for a woman with a garden. His ember is no bigger than a seed.

story: Oswin walked for forty years and stopped for a woman with a garden. His ember is nearly out.

quests.summary: The ember tugs towards a village, and another light in it, very small.
quests.title: The Settled Wayfarer

lines.text: Our people in the far villages think the walls have fallen. Tell them they haven't.
You've their grey. Walk through the heir's camp as one of his, and nobody will look twice.

steps.objective: Hear the warden out at the stone.
story: The warden asked me to carry word through the heir's lines that the Grass Kingdom stands.

done.text: Through the tents in grey. Nobody looks twice.

steps.objective: Walk through the heir's camp in their grey, to its far side.
story: I walked through the heir's camp in their grey, and nobody looked twice.

lines.text: At the last fire beyond the tents, a woman in ochre takes the message, and then your hand.
Linnet. Tell my brother I'm alive. He thinks the walls ate me too.
She means the heir.
He went looking for our grandfather's summer. I stayed for the people who lived through it.

steps.objective: Give the warden's message to whoever waits beyond the tents.

people.heirs_sister: Linnet, the heir's sister. She lives inside the Grass Kingdom's land, and wants him to know she's alive.

story: On the far side of the heir's camp a woman took the message: Linnet, the heir's sister, alive inside the kingdom's land.

words.heirs_sister: The heir's sister. She lives inside the Grass Kingdom's land, and wants him to know it.

quests.summary: The warden has a message for the kingdom's people beyond the heir's lines, and nobody who isn't in grey gets through.
quests.title: Through the Lines

arrived.text: Go home. There's nothing here for you.
...They turned him away too, didn't they? Your Wend.

lines.text: Hesper. I'm walking to the Keepers. Everyone says they'll take in anyone. Walk with me?

steps.objective: Walk Hesper to the Keepers' stronghold.
story: I walked Hesper the pilgrim to the Keepers' door. They turned her away, as they turned Wend.

quests.summary: A pilgrim on the road asks to walk with you to the Keepers.
quests.title: The Pilgrims

done.text: Three pages of orders, in three different hands, and all of them say the same thing.

steps.objective: Find the captains' pages in the Gazebound's outposts, and read them: {read}/{pages}.
story: The Gazebound's outposts keep their orders on paper, copied out by their captains. I've been collecting them.

lines.text: Where did you get those? ...Give them here.
He reads them by the fire, slowly. His jaw sets.
The heir's orders, in his captains' hands. I copied a few of these myself.
They're not hunting you. They're herding you.

steps.objective: Show the pages to Corin at the caravan.
story: Corin read the captains' pages. They're not hunting us, he says. They're herding us.

done.text: Two more pages, from beyond the sea. The same orders, and nearer now.

steps.objective: Find the captains' pages in the outposts beyond the sea, and read them: {read}/{pages}.
story: The outposts beyond the sea keep their orders too, copied from a page in the old captain's own hand.

steps.objective: Find the page the captains copied from, at the old captain's house in the dark wood.
story: In the house in the dark wood lay the page the captains copied from. It's in his hand.

lines.text: That's his hand. He wrote my orders for six winters. I'd know it anywhere.
He reads it twice, and then sits very still.
The bread, the following, the herding. All of it was his, before he ever lit his last fire.
Whatever's in that ember now, it learned from him.

steps.objective: Show the last page to Corin at the caravan.
story: Corin read the last page. The whole plan was his old captain's, written before his last fire.

quests.summary: A page of orders from a Gazebound outpost, copied out by one of their captains. Their other outposts may hold more.
quests.title: Captains' Pages

done.text: Word goes round the taverns: the traveller with the coal plays a fair game, and wins it.

steps.objective: Win games of bones in the taverns: {won}/{count}.
story: In the taverns they play bones for stakes. I've learned to stop while I'm ahead.

steps.objective: Play bones in the taverns whenever you like.
story: Word of my game goes ahead of me now.

done.text: The dicer pushes a folded chart across with the stakes. "Fair's fair. Somebody bet it to me once. I never had the legs for it."

lines.text: Word reaches you on the road: in the far taverns, a dicer plays for a chart.

steps.objective: Win a game of bones in a far tavern, where a dicer plays for a chart: {won}/{count}.

reward.claimed: You fold the chart into your pack.

items.name: A Dicer's Chart
items.tooltip: A door is marked on it, far out where the maps end.

reward.text: a chart with a door marked on it.
reward.title: A Dicer's Chart

story: In a far tavern I won a dicer's chart. A door is marked on it, far out where the maps end.

quests.summary: The taverns play bones for stakes, and somebody in every one of them will play a stranger. Win a few.
quests.title: The Dice

lines.text: That Frost Walker let me look at her knife once, while she camped with us. Twenty winters old. Not a fleck of rust on it.
Frost iron, she called it. Their smiths knew how to work it. I never learned.
My hammer cracked the night the town burned. Since then I mend everything halfway, and it shows.
Find me where they dug that metal, and I'll make a hammer worth the name. Then bring me anything.
They'd have dug it near their hall. You don't haul ore through deep snow.

steps.objective: Hear Hob out at the caravan: right-click him.

people.hob: His hammer cracked the night Tollbridge burned, and since then he mends only halfway. He wants the Frost Walkers' metal for a new one.

story: Hob wants the Frost Walkers' metal, frost iron, to make a hammer worth the name. They'd have dug it near their hall.

words.frost_iron: The Frost Walkers' metal. Nell's knife was made of it: twenty winters old, and not a fleck of rust.

clues.text: An old ore cart, half buried in the snow, still loaded with dark stone. Its iron bands are as bright as the day they were forged.
Under the snow, two grooves worn into the rock, a cart's width apart, running off into the drifts.

done.text: Carts went this way for a long time.

steps.objective: Look round the Frost Walkers' stair for where they hauled their ore: {found}/{needed}.
story: By the stair to the Frost Walkers' hall lay an old ore cart, and ruts worn into the rock ran off into the snow.

done.text: The ruts end at a frame of black timber over a square shaft. A windlass, its rope long rotted.
Cold air breathes up out of the dark.

steps.objective: Follow the ruts into the snow.
story: The ruts led to the Frost Walkers' old mine: a shaft going down into the dark.

done.text: The drift ends in a wall that isn't rock: dressed black stone, older than anything above, broken through in the middle.
Something soft and dark has grown over the old wall. It twitches when you breathe.
In the stone round the break, pale metal glints.

lines.text: Ladders go down the shaft wall, landing after landing, into the dark.

steps.objective: Climb down the shaft and follow the drift to its end. Bring light.
story: At the bottom of their mine the Frost Walkers had dug up to a wall older than anything above, black stone grown over with something that twitches. They stopped there.

steps.objective: Dig the pale metal with an iron pickaxe: {carried}/{count}.
steps.shriek: Something behind the old wall shrieks. The sound goes down and down, a long way. Nothing answers.
story: I dug the Frost Walkers' metal out of the stone by the old wall. It's cold, and it stays cold.

words.frost_iron: It lies in the deep stone at the bottom of their mine, by a wall older than anything above. It stays cold in the hand, and no common fire melts it.

done.text: That's it. Cold as the day it came out of the rock.
Leave it with me tonight.

steps.objective: Hold four lumps of frost iron out to Hob at the caravan: right-click him with them in your hand.
steps.short: Four lumps, and I'll have my hammer. That's not four.
story: I brought Hob four lumps of frost iron. He's making himself a hammer worth the name.

done.text: There. A hammer worth the name. Bring me anything.

steps.objective: Sleep: Hob works through the night.

people.hob: Since the Frost Walkers' metal he has a hammer worth the name. He makes anything whole overnight, makes it again in frost iron, and sets an old book's writing into steel.

story: Hob worked through the night. Now he makes anything whole, makes it again in frost iron, and sets the old books into steel.

quests.summary: Hob wants a word about the Frost Walkers' metal. He's at the caravan in the evenings.
quests.title: The Lost Ore

steps.objective: Go and look at the old camp.

clues.text: A tin box under the stones. Inside, a coal no bigger than a thumb, black and cold. An ember, gone out.
A journal, swollen with rain. It is signed with a circle cut through by a line: the mark from the tunnels.
Something heavy in old cloth: a carved stone, cut down to fit a pack. It hums faintly at your touch.

done.text: The journal's last page reads: "One more winter here. The ember is so small now. I'll walk in spring."
They didn't. Spring doesn't come for someone who stops. Take the stone. They'd want it walked.

steps.objective: Search the old camp: {found}/{needed}.

reward.claimed: You wrap the stone in its cloth again and pack it, with the journal.
reward.text: a stone of one's own, cut down to fit a pack, and the journal it was left with.
reward.title: Their Stone

story: In an old camp by the road I found another Wayfarer's ember, gone out, and their journal. They stopped walking, and their ember went home. They left their stone. I carry it now.

words.stone: A stone of my own, cut down to fit a pack. Set down and touched, it folds me back to it from any waystone I've touched, and the ember burns the walk it saves.

quests.summary: An old camp by the road, and the voice wants me to look at it. Somebody sat there too long.
quests.title: The Cache

done.text: She's mine? She's really mine?
Bramble. Her name's Bramble.
Pip leads Bramble to Agna's tent, and Agna pretends not to smile.

lines.text: In the stories every Wayfarer has a horse. Find me one? A brown one.

steps.name: Bramble
steps.objective: Find Pip a horse and bring it to the caravan's fire.

people.pip: Pip wanted a horse, like the Wayfarers in the stories. I found one, and Pip called her Bramble.

story: I brought Pip a horse. Pip called her Bramble, and she grazes by Agna's tent now.

quests.summary: Pip wants a horse, like the Wayfarers in the stories. Any horse will do, Pip says, as long as it's brown.
quests.title: The Road

steps.awake: Not yet. Sit by the fire a while.

choices.reply: Then I'll follow your smoke, and wait at the edge of it.
choices.story: I told Bram we'd bring Davy back.

lines.text: A man with a herder's crook walks out of the dark and stops at the edge of the light.
Bram. I kept sheep, up the valley. Three nights back the grey coats took my boy. Davy. He's eleven.
At the edge of the light, Corin looks away. "Eleven. They'll have marked him by now."
Their outpost's a day on, the way you're going. I'm no good with a blade. Please.

steps.objective: Sit at the caravan's fire.

people.bram: A herder. The Gazebound took his son Davy to their outpost a day ahead.

story: A herder named Bram came to our fire. The Gazebound took his son Davy to their outpost a day ahead.

done.text: A wooden tower over the trees, and a banner with an open eye on it.

steps.objective: Find the Gazebound outpost a day ahead.
story: The outpost where they keep Bram's son stands a day ahead of the caravan.

lines.text: The ember! Hold them off the boy!

steps.objective: Hold against the outpost's men.
story: The outpost's men came down on us, and we held.

lines.text: A boy in grey sits at the foot of the tower. Nobody is guarding him.
Davy. Did Da send you? ...Is he angry?
He pulls his collar aside. Over his heart, a cut that has only just closed.
They said the night won't look at me now. It doesn't. Things walk right past me.

steps.objective: Find Bram's son at the outpost.

people.bram_son: Bram's son Davy. The Gazebound gave him their scar, and the night's creatures walk past him now.

story: We found Bram's son Davy at the foot of the outpost. They'd given him their scar. The night's creatures walk past him now.

arrived.text: Is Da here? ...He'll come. He always comes when it's dark.

lines.text: Davy gets up and follows you. He doesn't look back at the tower.

steps.objective: Walk Davy back to the caravan.
story: I walked Davy back to the caravan.

done.text: Davy sits at the edge of the light, watching the dark for his father.

steps.objective: Bring Davy to the caravan's fire.
story: Davy waited at our fire for his father.

lines.text: Bram comes in out of the dark. He holds his son a long time. Over the boy's shoulder he looks at the fire, at the dark, anywhere but at the scar.
Sit down, Davy. ...No. Over there, where I can see you.
We'll camp with you, if you'll have us. I can mind animals. It's all I can do.

steps.objective: Sit with Bram at the caravan's fire.

people.bram: Bram got his son back. He camps with us now, and can't look at the scar.

story: Bram and Davy camp with us now.

quests.summary: A herder came to the caravan's fire: the Gazebound took his son to their outpost a day ahead. Bring the boy back.
quests.title: Bram's Son

lines.text: Wayfarers in the stories can tell who walked by from one footprint. Can you teach me?
A fox goes past our camp every night. I bet its den's close. Take me? Please?

steps.objective: Hear Pip out at the fire.
story: Pip asked me to teach them to read tracks. A fox goes past our camp every night, and its den is close.

arrived.text: There! Its hole. And its prints go on from here. Show me how you read them.

lines.text: I'll be quiet. I'm always quiet.

steps.objective: Take Pip to the fox's den a little way ahead.
story: I took Pip to the fox's den.

clues.text: Pip crouches at the hole. "It's warm in there. Something's asleep."
Pip puts a finger in the print. "Four toes, no claws dragging. A fox. Walking, not running."
Pip looks from one print to the next. "Only one set. It was alone. And it wasn't scared of anything."

done.text: Pip sits back on their heels, grinning, with dirt on their nose.

steps.objective: Read the prints with Pip, with the ember held up: {found}/{needed}.
story: Pip read the fox's prints with me: alone, walking, not running, asleep now in its den.

done.text: Tamsin! A fox went by, walking, not running, all on its own, and it's asleep now. I read it in the dirt!
Did you, now. Then you can read me where the sheep went tomorrow.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: Pip told the whole caravan about the fox.

quests.summary: Pip wants to learn to read tracks, like the Wayfarers in the stories. There's a fox's den a little way ahead.
quests.title: Tracks

lines.text: There's a rite at the outpost ahead. Tonight, or near it. Novices take the scar there.
I took mine at fifteen. Go and look, if you want to know what we are. I won't.

steps.objective: Hear Corin out at the fire.
story: Corin told me of a rite at an outpost ahead, where the Gazebound's novices take the scar.

done.text: You're too late. The rite is over, and the outpost is quiet.
A boy in grey lies on his back at the foot of the tower. He isn't breathing.

lines.text: Quietly, now. They don't like to be watched at it.

steps.objective: Find the outpost where the rite is held. Keep low.
story: I went to see the rite, and came too late. A novice lay dead at the foot of the tower.

clues.text: A ring of burnt earth and spent candles. Ash in the middle, and the marks of many feet round it.
His grey coat is open. Over his heart, a cut that never closed. Whatever looked in didn't let go.

done.text: Nobody comes back for him. They leave the ones the night doesn't let go.

steps.objective: Look at what the rite left, with the ember held up: {found}/{needed}.
story: The rite opens a novice's chest for the night to look in. This one didn't live through it.

done.text: Fifteen? Fair hair? ...Tobin. His mother cooked for our company.
They'll tell her he was found unworthy. They called it a blessing, when it took my friend.
Nobody at the fire knew him. You tell them what you saw, and that is all the burial he gets.

steps.objective: Make for their smoke.
story: The dead novice was fifteen. Whatever looked into him didn't let go.

quests.summary: Corin heard there's a rite tonight at an outpost ahead, where the Gazebound's novices take the scar. Go and see it.
quests.title: The Scar of the Searched

lines.text: The sand people say there's a horse on the plains ahead that never sleeps. It just stands there and watches.
In the stories a horse like that waits for one rider. Go and see if it's you?

steps.objective: Hear Pip out at the fire.
story: Pip heard of a horse on the grass ahead that never sleeps, and asked me to go and see it.

done.text: A white horse stands alone, its head already turned your way. As you come it follows you, and doesn't stop.

steps.objective: Find the white horse ahead.
story: Ahead of us stands a white horse that never sleeps. It watches whoever is nearest, and never looks away.

done.text: It stands at the edge of the firelight, watching you. The other animals keep away from it.
Doesn't blink, that one. Something's looked into it and gone again, I'd say.

steps.objective: Tame the white horse, and ride it to the caravan's fire.
story: I tamed the white horse. It never sleeps, and it runs like nothing else on the road.

quests.summary: Pip heard of a horse ahead that never sleeps, and never stops watching. Find it, and tame it if you can.
quests.title: The Horse That Never Sleeps

done.text: Grey stone, and blue light, and a quiet so deep your own breathing sounds loud.
At the city's heart stands a frame of black stone, taller than a house. A lectern waits before it.

lines.text: Under the hills ahead, little light, lies the city that built the first gate. Dig, if you want to see it.
Walk softly down there. Their guard still listens.

steps.objective: Dig down to the city under the hills, and walk softly.
story: The gaze told me of a city under the hills, the one that built the first gate.

steps.objective: Read the book on the lectern at the city's heart.
story: By the city's gate lay its archivist's last record. What came through that gate isn't the dragon's, and it is still coming.

quests.summary: The gaze says the city that built the first gate lies under the hills ahead. Go down to it.
quests.title: The First Gate

done.text: Bones on the rock, bleached, with dead brush woven through them. It stinks of the things.

lines.text: At dawn the phantoms that hunted you in the night drop away, all of them towards the same height ahead.

steps.objective: Find where the phantoms nest, on the height ahead.
story: The phantoms nest on a height ahead, in a ring of bones.

lines.text: The nest is empty by day. Whatever lives in it comes back with the dark.

steps.name: The nest's mother
steps.objective: Wait at the nest for night, and kill the nest's mother.

rises.text: Something lifts off the rock below the nest, far too big, and turns towards you.

story: A phantom four times the size of the others rose from the nest. I killed it, and burned the nest. Fewer of them hunt the sky now.

won.text: The nest's mother falls onto the rock and lies still.
You set the brush alight. The bones crack in the heat, and the smoke goes up a long way.

quests.summary: At dawn the phantoms drop away towards one height ahead. Find their nest, and burn it.
quests.title: The Phantom Nest

choices.reply: ...I'd look after it. I would. I'd keep walking.
choices.story: I told Pip that if it comes to that, the ember is theirs.
choices.text: If it comes to that, it's yours.

choices.reply: Oh. ...Good. I don't want it anyway. I want you to come back.
choices.story: I told Pip the ember goes in the ground with me.
choices.text: It goes in the ground with me.

lines.text: Can I ask you something? If you die out there. What happens to it?
In the stories the Wayfarer gives the light to someone first. So it doesn't go out.

steps.objective: Hear Pip out at the fire.
story: Pip asked what happens to the ember if I die out there.

quests.summary: Pip has a question about the ember, and has been working up to it for days. Hear it at the fire.
quests.title: Pip's Ember

done.text: You wake in a bed under your own roof. Nobody is watching. Nothing is coming.

lines.text: The sky is empty. For the first time since the old man's fire, you can stop.

steps.objective: Build a home, and sleep in a bed under its roof.
story: The gaze is gone. I built a home, and slept in a bed of my own.

quests.summary: The gaze is gone. Nothing comes at night that you don't let in, and seeds take root again. Build a home.
quests.title: A Home

done.text: You wake in a bed under your own roof, grown, with an ember of your own. Nothing is watching.

lines.text: Years later. You are Pip, grown, and the coal in your hands never went out.

steps.objective: Build a home, and sleep in a bed under its roof.
story: The one I followed is gone. They walked into the frame and the dark closed behind them.
I carry the ember now. I built us a home, like I said I would.

quests.summary: The one Pip followed walked into the frame, and the dark closed behind them. Pip carries the ember now. Build a home.
quests.title: Pip's Road

done.text: Where your people last made camp, the night is empty. Nobody keeps watch, and nobody needs to.
Out past its edge, something waits in the dark, and doesn't come any closer.

steps.objective: Go home, to where your people last made camp.
story: The gaze kept its promise. Where my people sleep, nothing comes at night. Everywhere else, it hunts.

quests.summary: The gaze kept its promise: where your people sleep, nothing comes at night. Everywhere else, it sees, and its creatures hunt. Go home.
quests.title: The Promised Home
